flags.name: action_cache
flags.doc: Dump action cache content.

flags.name: action_cache_store_output_metadata
flags.doc: no-op

flags.name: action_env
flags.doc:
Specifies the set of environment variables available to actions with target
configuration. Variables can be either specified by `name`, in which case
the value will be taken from the invocation environment, by the `name=value`
pair which sets the value independent of the invocation environment, or by
`=name`, which unsets the variable of that name. This option can be used
multiple times; for options given for the same variable, the latest wins,
options for different variables accumulate.

Note that unless `--incompatible_repo_env_ignores_action_env` is true, all `name=value`
pairs will be available to repository rules.

flags.name: adb
flags.doc: adb binary to use for the 'mobile-install' command. If unspecified, the one in the Android SDK specified by the --android_sdk_channel command line option (or  the default SDK if --android_sdk_channel is not specified) is used.

flags.name: adb_arg
flags.doc: Extra arguments to pass to adb. Usually used to designate a device to install to.

flags.name: add_go_exec_groups_to_binary_rules
flags.doc: When enabled, 'go_build' and 'go_link' execution groups are added to binary rules like 'cc_binary'.

flags.name: all
flags.doc:
Fetches all external repositories necessary for building any target or repository.
This is the default if no other flags and arguments are provided. Only works
when `--enable_bzlmod` is on.

flags.name: all_repos
flags.doc: For `mod show_repo`: display all repos in the entire workspace.

flags.name: all_visible_repos
flags.doc: For `mod show_repo`: display all repos visible to the chosen base module, under their apparent names.

flags.name: allow_analysis_cache_discard
flags.doc:
If discarding the analysis cache due to a change in the build system, setting this
option to false will cause bazel to exit, rather than continuing with the build.
This option has no effect when `--discard_analysis_cache` is also set.

flags.name: allow_analysis_failures
flags.doc:
If true, an analysis failure of a rule target results in the target's propagation
of an instance of `AnalysisFailureInfo` containing the error description, instead
of resulting in a build failure.

flags.name: allow_experimental_loads
flags.doc: If enabled, issue only a warning instead of an error for loads of experimental .bzls.

flags.name: allow_local_tests
flags.doc: If true, Bazel will allow local tests to run.

flags.name: allow_one_action_on_resource_unavailable
flags.doc: If set, allow at least one action to run even if the resource is not enough or unavailable.

flags.name: allow_unresolved_symlinks
flags.doc:
If enabled, Bazel allows the use of `ctx.action.declare_symlink()` and the use of
`ctx.actions.symlink()` without a target file, thus allowing the creation of
unresolved symlinks.

Unresolved symlinks inside tree artifacts are not currently supported.

flags.name: allow_yanked_versions
flags.doc:
Specified the module versions in the form of
`{module1}@{version1},module2@{version2}` that will be allowed in the resolved
dependency graph even if they are declared yanked in the registry where they come
from (if they are not coming from a [`NonRegistryOverride`]).
Otherwise, yanked versions will cause the resolution to fail. You can also define allowed
yanked versions with the `BZLMOD_ALLOW_YANKED_VERSIONS` environment variable. You can
disable this check by using the keyword `all` (not recommended).

[`NonRegistryOverride`]: https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/master/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/bazel/bzlmod/NonRegistryOverride.java

flags.name: allowed_cpu_values
flags.doc: Allowed values for the `--cpu` flag.

flags.name: allowed_local_actions_regex
flags.doc: A regex whitelist for action types which may be run locally. If unset, all actions are allowed to execute locally

flags.name: allowed_strategies_by_exec_platform
flags.doc:
Filters spawn strategies by the execution platform without affecting order.
For example:
```
common --spawn_strategy=remote,sandboxed,worker,local
common --strategy=Genrule=local
common --allowed_strategies_by_exec_platform=@platforms//host:host=local,sandboxed,worker
common --allowed_strategies_by_exec_platform=//:linux_amd64=remote
```
With the above options;
- Actions configured for the host platform will be given `remote,sandboxed,worker`.
- Actions configured for the `//:linux_amd64` platform will be given `remote`.
- Actions configured for the `//:linux_amd64` platform with mnemonic `Genrule` will be
  given no strategies and fail to spawn.

flags.name: always_profile_slow_operations
flags.doc: Whether profiling slow operations is always turned on

flags.name: analysis_testing_deps_limit
flags.doc:
Sets the maximum number of transitive dependencies through a rule attribute with
a `for_analysis_testing` configuration transition.
Exceeding this limit will result in a rule error.

flags.name: analyze
flags.doc:
Execute the loading/analysis phase; this is the usual behaviour. Specifying `--noanalyze`
causes the build to stop before starting the loading/analysis phase, just doing
target pattern parsing and returning zero if that completed successfully; this
mode is useful for testing.

flags.name: android_compiler
flags.doc: The Android target compiler.

flags.name: android_cpu
flags.doc: No-op
flags.deprecationWarning: Legacy Android flags have been deprecated. See https://blog.bazel.build/2023/11/15/android-platforms.html for details and migration directions

flags.name: android_crosstool_top
flags.doc: No-op
flags.deprecationWarning: Legacy Android flags have been deprecated. See https://blog.bazel.build/2023/11/15/android-platforms.html for details and migration directions

flags.name: android_databinding_use_androidx
flags.doc: Generate AndroidX-compatible data-binding files. This is only used with databinding v2. This flag is a no-op.

flags.name: android_databinding_use_v3_4_args
flags.doc: Use android databinding v2 with 3.4.0 argument. This flag is a no-op.

flags.name: android_dynamic_mode
flags.doc: Determines whether C++ deps of Android rules will be linked dynamically when a cc_binary does not explicitly create a shared library. 'default' means bazel will choose whether to link dynamically.  'fully' means all libraries will be linked dynamically. 'off' means that all libraries will be linked in mostly static mode.

flags.name: android_fixed_resource_neverlinking
flags.doc: If true, resources will properly not get propagated through neverlinked libraries. Otherwise, the old behavior of propagating those resources if no resource-related attributes are specified in the neverlink library will be preserved.

flags.name: android_grte_top
flags.doc: No-op
flags.deprecationWarning: Legacy Android flags have been deprecated. See https://blog.bazel.build/2023/11/15/android-platforms.html for details and migration directions

flags.name: android_manifest_merger
flags.doc: Selects the manifest merger to use for android_binary rules. Flag to help the transition to the Android manifest merger from the legacy merger.

flags.name: android_manifest_merger_order
flags.doc: Sets the order of manifests passed to the manifest merger for Android binaries. ALPHABETICAL means manifests are sorted by path relative to the execroot. ALPHABETICAL_BY_CONFIGURATION means manifests are sorted by paths relative to the configuration directory within the output directory. DEPENDENCY means manifests are ordered with each library's manifest coming before the manifests of its dependencies.

flags.name: android_migration_tag_check
flags.doc: If enabled, strict usage of the Starlark migration tag is enabled for android rules. Prefer using --incompatible_disable_native_android_rules.

flags.name: android_platforms
flags.doc: Sets the platforms that android_binary targets use. If multiple platforms are specified, then the binary is a fat APKs, which contains native binaries for each specified target platform.

flags.name: android_resource_shrinking
flags.doc: Enables resource shrinking for android_binary APKs that use ProGuard.

flags.name: android_sdk
flags.doc: No-op
flags.deprecationWarning: Legacy Android flags have been deprecated. See https://blog.bazel.build/2023/11/15/android-platforms.html for details and migration directions

flags.name: announce
flags.doc: Deprecated. No-op.
flags.deprecationWarning: This option is now deprecated and is a no-op

flags.name: announce_rc
flags.doc: Whether to announce rc options.

flags.name: apk_signing_method
flags.doc: Implementation to use to sign APKs

flags.name: apple_crosstool_top
flags.doc: No-op

flags.name: apple_generate_dsym
flags.doc: Whether to generate debug symbol(.dSYM) file(s).

flags.name: apple_platform_type
flags.doc: Don't set this value from the command line - it is derived from other flags and configuration transitions derived from rule attributes

flags.name: apple_platforms
flags.doc: Comma-separated list of platforms to use when building Apple binaries.

flags.name: apple_split_cpu
flags.doc: Don't set this value from the command line - it is derived from other flags and configuration transitions derived from rule attributes

flags.name: archived_tree_artifact_mnemonics_filter
flags.doc: Regex filter for mnemonics of actions for which we should create archived tree artifacts. This option is a no-op for actions which do not generate tree artifacts.

flags.name: aspect_deps
flags.doc: How to resolve aspect dependencies when the output format is one of {xml,proto,record}. 'off' means no aspect dependencies are resolved, 'conservative' (the default) means all declared aspect dependencies are added regardless of whether they are given the rule class of direct dependencies, 'precise' means that only those aspects are added that are possibly active given the rule class of the direct dependencies. Note that precise mode requires loading other packages to evaluate a single target thus making it slower than the other modes. Also note that even precise mode is not completely precise: the decision whether to compute an aspect is decided in the analysis phase, which is not run during 'bazel query'.

flags.name: aspects
flags.doc:
Comma-separated list of aspects to be applied to top-level targets. In the list, if
aspect `some_aspect` specifies required aspect providers via
`required_aspect_providers`, `some_aspect` will run after
every aspect that was mentioned before it in the aspects list whose advertised
providers satisfy `some_aspect` required aspect providers. Moreover,
`some_aspect` will run after all its required aspects specified by
`requires` attribute.
`some_aspect` will then have access to the values of those aspects'
providers.
`{bzl-file-label}%{aspect_name}`, for example `//tools:my_def.bzl%my_aspect`, where
`my_aspect` is a top-level value from a file `tools/my_def.bzl`.

flags.name: aspects_parameters
flags.doc:
Specifies the values of the command-line aspects parameters. Each parameter value is
specified via `<param_name>=<param_value>`, for example `my_param=my_val` where
`my_param` is a parameter of some aspect in `--aspects` list or required by an
aspect in the list. This option can be used multiple times. However, it is not
allowed to assign values to the same parameter more than once.

flags.name: async
flags.doc: If true, output cleaning is asynchronous. When this command completes, it will be safe to execute new commands in the same client, even though the deletion may continue in the background.

flags.name: attempt_to_print_relative_paths
flags.doc: When printing the location part of messages, attempt to use a path relative to the workspace directory or one of the directories specified by --package_path.

flags.name: auto_cpu_environment_group
flags.doc: No-op

flags.name: auto_output_filter
flags.doc: If --output_filter is not specified, then the value for this option is used create a filter automatically. Allowed values are 'none' (filter nothing / show everything), 'all' (filter everything / show nothing), 'packages' (include output from rules in packages mentioned on the Blaze command line), and 'subpackages' (like 'packages', but also include subpackages). For the 'packages' and 'subpackages' values //java/foo and //javatests/foo are treated as one package)'.

flags.name: autodetect_server_javabase
flags.doc: When --noautodetect_server_javabase is passed, Bazel does not fall back to the local JDK for running the bazel server and instead exits.

flags.name: base_module
flags.doc: Specify a module relative to which the specified target repos will be interpreted.

flags.name: batch
flags.doc: If set, Bazel will be run as just a client process without a server, instead of in the standard client/server mode. This is deprecated and will be removed, please prefer shutting down the server explicitly if you wish to avoid lingering servers.

flags.name: batch_cpu_scheduling
flags.doc: Only on Linux; use 'batch' CPU scheduling for Blaze. This policy is useful for workloads that are non-interactive, but do not want to lower their nice value. See 'man 2 sched_setscheduler'. If false, then Bazel does not perform a system call.

flags.name: bazelrc
flags.doc:
The location of the user .bazelrc file containing default values of Bazel options.
`/dev/null` indicates that all further `--bazelrc`s will be ignored, which is useful to
disable the search for a user rc file, e.g. in release builds.

This option can also be specified multiple times. e.g. with
`--bazelrc=x.rc --bazelrc=y.rc --bazelrc=/dev/null --bazelrc=z.rc`.
1. `x.rc` and `y.rc` are read.
2. `z.rc` is ignored due to the prior `/dev/null`.
If unspecified, Bazel uses the first `.bazelrc` file it finds in
the following two locations: the workspace directory, then the user's home
directory.

Note: command line options will always supersede any option in bazelrc.

flags.name: bep_maximum_open_remote_upload_files
flags.doc: Maximum number of open files allowed during BEP artifact upload.

flags.name: bes_backend
flags.doc:
Specifies the build event service (BES) backend endpoint in the form
`[SCHEME://]HOST[:PORT]`. The default is to disable BES uploads. Supported schemes
are `grpc` and `grpcs` (grpc with TLS enabled). If no scheme is provided, Bazel
assumes `grpcs`.

flags.name: bes_best_effort
flags.doc: No-op
flags.deprecationWarning: BES best effort upload has been removed. The flag has no more functionality attached to it and will be removed in a future release.

flags.name: bes_check_preceding_lifecycle_events
flags.doc:
Sets the field `check_preceding_lifecycle_events_present` on
`PublishBuildToolEventStreamRequest` which tells BES to check whether it previously
received `InvocationAttemptStarted` and `BuildEnqueued` events matching the current
tool event.

flags.name: bes_header
flags.doc:
Specify a header in `NAME=VALUE` form that will be included in BES requests.
Multiple headers can be passed by specifying the flag multiple times. Multiple
values for the same name will be converted to a comma-separated list.

flags.name: bes_instance_name
flags.doc: Specifies the instance name under which the BES will persist uploaded BEP. Defaults to null.

flags.name: bes_keywords
flags.doc:
Specifies a list of notification keywords to be added the default set of keywords
published to BES (`command_name={command_name}`, `protocol_name=BEP`).
Defaults to none.

flags.name: bes_lifecycle_events
flags.doc: Specifies whether to publish BES lifecycle events. (defaults to 'true').

flags.name: bes_oom_finish_upload_timeout
flags.doc: Specifies how long bazel should wait for the BES/BEP upload to complete while OOMing. This flag ensures termination when the JVM is severely GC thrashing and cannot make progress on any user thread.

flags.name: bes_outerr_buffer_size
flags.doc:
Specifies the maximal size of stdout or stderr to be buffered in BEP, before it is
reported as a progress event. Individual writes are still reported in a single
event, even if larger than the specified value up to `--bes_outerr_chunk_size`.

flags.name: bes_outerr_chunk_size
flags.doc: Specifies the maximal size of stdout or stderr to be sent to BEP in a single message.

flags.name: bes_proxy
flags.doc:
Connect to the Build Event Service through a proxy. Currently this flag can only be
used to configure a Unix domain socket (`unix:/path/to/socket`).

flags.name: bes_results_url
flags.doc: Specifies the base URL where a user can view the information streamed to the BES backend. Bazel will output the URL appended by the invocation id to the terminal.

flags.name: bes_system_keywords
flags.doc:
Specifies a list of notification keywords to be included directly, without the
`user_keyword=` prefix included for keywords supplied via `--bes_keywords`.
Intended for Build service operators that set `--bes_lifecycle_events=false` and
include keywords when calling `PublishLifecycleEvent`. Build service operators
using this flag should prevent users from overriding the flag value.

flags.name: bes_timeout
flags.doc:
Specifies how long bazel should wait for the BES/BEP upload to complete after the
build and tests have finished. A valid timeout is a natural number followed by a
unit: Days (d), hours (h), minutes (m), seconds (s), and milliseconds (ms). The
default value is `0` which means that there is no timeout.

flags.name: bes_upload_mode
flags.doc:
Specifies whether the Build Event Service upload should block the build completion or
should end the invocation immediately and finish the upload in the
background.
- `wait_for_upload_complete`: blocks at the end of the current invocation until
  all events (including lifecycle events if applicable) are uploaded and
  acknowledged by the backend.
- `nowait_for_upload_complete`: blocks at the beginning of the next invocation
  until all events (including lifecycle events if applicable) are uploaded and
  acknowledged by the backend.
- `fully_async`: blocks at the beginning of the next invocation until all events
  are uploaded but does not wait for acknowledgements. Events may be lost in case
  of (transient) failures and backends may report streams as incomplete in this
  mode. There is no guarantee that `FinishInvocationAttempt` or `FinishBuild`
  lifecycle events are sent.

flags.name: binary_path
flags.doc: The absolute path of the bazel binary.

flags.name: block_for_lock
flags.doc: When --noblock_for_lock is passed, Bazel does not wait for a running command to complete, but instead exits immediately.

flags.name: break_build_on_parallel_dex2oat_failure
flags.doc: If true dex2oat action failures will cause the build to break instead of executing dex2oat during test runtime.

flags.name: build
flags.doc:
Execute the build; this is the usual behaviour.
Specifying `--nobuild` causes the build to stop before executing the build
actions, returning zero if the package loading and analysis phases completed
successfully; this mode is useful for testing those phases.

flags.name: build_event_binary_file
flags.doc:
If non-empty, write a varint delimited binary representation of representation of the
build event protocol to that file. This option implies
`--bes_upload_mode=wait_for_upload_complete`.

flags.name: build_event_binary_file_path_conversion
flags.doc:
Convert paths in the binary file representation of the build event protocol to more
globally valid URIs whenever possible; if disabled, the `file://` uri scheme will
always be used

flags.name: build_event_binary_file_upload_mode
flags.doc:
Specifies whether the Build Event Service upload for `--build_event_binary_file` should
block the build completion or should end the invocation immediately and finish
the upload in the background. Either `wait_for_upload_complete` (default),
`nowait_for_upload_complete`, or `fully_async`.

flags.name: build_event_json_file
flags.doc:
If non-empty, write a JSON serialisation of the build event protocol to that file.
This option implies `--bes_upload_mode=wait_for_upload_complete`.

flags.name: build_event_json_file_path_conversion
flags.doc:
Convert paths in the json file representation of the build event protocol to more
globally valid URIs whenever possible; if disabled, the `file://` uri scheme will
always be used

flags.name: build_event_json_file_upload_mode
flags.doc:
Specifies whether the Build Event Service upload for `--build_event_json_file` should
block the build completion or should end the invocation immediately and finish
the upload in the background. Either `wait_for_upload_complete` (default),
`nowait_for_upload_complete`, or `fully_async`.

flags.name: build_event_max_named_set_of_file_entries
flags.doc:
The maximum number of entries for a single `named_set_of_files` event; values smaller
than 2 are ignored and no event splitting is performed. This is intended for
limiting the maximum event size in the build event protocol, although it does not
directly control event size. The total event size is a function of the structure
of the set as well as the file and uri lengths, which may in turn depend on the
hash function.

flags.name: build_event_publish_all_actions
flags.doc: Whether all actions should be published.

flags.name: build_event_text_file
flags.doc: If non-empty, write a textual representation of the build event protocol to that file

flags.name: build_event_text_file_path_conversion
flags.doc:
Convert paths in the text file representation of the build event protocol to more
globally valid URIs whenever possible; if disabled, the `file://` uri scheme will
always be used

flags.name: build_event_text_file_upload_mode
flags.doc:
Specifies whether the Build Event Service upload for `--build_event_text_file` should
block the build completion or should end the invocation immediately and finish
the upload in the background. Either `wait_for_upload_complete` (default),
`nowait_for_upload_complete`, or `fully_async`.

flags.name: build_event_upload_max_retries
flags.doc: The maximum number of times Bazel should retry uploading a build event.

flags.name: build_manual_tests
flags.doc: Forces test targets tagged 'manual' to be built. 'manual' tests are excluded from processing. This option forces them to be built (but not executed).

flags.name: build_metadata
flags.doc: Custom key-value string pairs to supply in a build event.

flags.name: build_python_zip
flags.doc: Deprecated. No-op.
flags.deprecationWarning: The '--no' prefix is no longer supported for this flag. Please use --build_python_zip=false instead.

flags.name: build_request_id
flags.doc: Unique string identifier for the build being run.

flags.name: build_runfile_links
flags.doc: If true, build runfiles symlink forests for all targets.  If false, write them only when required by a local action, test or run command.

flags.name: build_runfile_manifests
flags.doc: If true, write runfiles manifests for all targets. If false, omit them. Local tests will fail to run when false.

flags.name: build_tag_filters
flags.doc: Specifies a comma-separated list of tags. Each tag can be optionally preceded with '-' to specify excluded tags. Only those targets will be built that contain at least one included tag and do not contain any excluded tags. This option does not affect the set of tests executed with the 'test' command; those are be governed by the test filtering options, for example '--test_tag_filters'

flags.name: build_test_dwp
flags.doc: If enabled, when building C++ tests statically and with fission the .dwp file  for the test binary will be automatically built as well.

flags.name: build_tests_only
flags.doc: If specified, only *_test and test_suite rules will be built and other targets specified on the command line will be ignored. By default everything that was requested will be built.

flags.name: bytecode_optimization_pass_actions
flags.doc: Do not use.

flags.name: bytecode_optimizers
flags.doc: Do not use.

flags.name: cache_computed_file_digests
flags.doc: If greater than 0, configures Bazel to cache file digests in memory based on their metadata instead of recomputing the digests from disk every time they are needed. Setting this to 0 ensures correctness because not all file changes can be noted from file metadata. When not 0, the number indicates the size of the cache as the number of file digests to be cached.

flags.name: cache_test_results
flags.doc:
If set to `auto`, Bazel reruns a test if and only if:
1. Bazel detects changes in the test or its dependencies,
2. The test is marked as `external`,
3. Multiple test runs were requested with `--runs_per_test`, or
4. The test previously failed.
If set to `yes`, Bazel caches all test results except for tests marked as
`external`. If set to `no`, Bazel does not cache any test results.

flags.name: canonicalize_policy
flags.doc: Output the canonical policy, after expansion and filtering. To keep the output clean, the canonicalized command arguments will NOT be shown when this option is set to true. Note that the command specified by --for_command affects the filtered policy, and if none is specified, the default command is 'build'.

flags.name: catalyst_cpus
flags.doc: Comma-separated list of architectures for which to build Apple Catalyst binaries.

flags.name: cc_dotd_files
flags.doc: Whether to generate and analyze .d files.

flags.name: cc_include_scanning
flags.doc: Whether to narrow inputs to C/C++ compilation by parsing #include lines from input files. This can improve performance and incrementality by decreasing the size of compilation input trees. However, it can also break builds because the include scanner does not fully implement C preprocessor semantics. In particular, it does not understand dynamic #include directives and ignores preprocessor conditional logic. Use at your own risk. Any issues relating to this flag that are filed will be closed. At Google without this flag your build will most likely fail.

flags.name: cc_output_directory_tag
flags.doc: Specifies a suffix to be added to the configuration directory.

flags.name: cc_proto_library_header_suffixes
flags.doc: Sets the suffixes of header files that a cc_proto_library creates.

flags.name: cc_proto_library_source_suffixes
flags.doc: Sets the suffixes of source files that a cc_proto_library creates.

flags.name: charset
flags.doc:
Chooses the character set to use for the tree. Only affects text output. Valid values
are `utf8` or `ascii`. Default is `utf8`

flags.name: check_bazel_compatibility
flags.doc: Check bazel version compatibility of Bazel modules. Valid values are `error` to escalate it to a resolution failure, `off` to disable the check, or `warning` to print a warning when mismatch detected.

flags.name: check_bzl_visibility
flags.doc: If disabled, .bzl load visibility errors are demoted to warnings.

flags.name: check_direct_dependencies
flags.doc: Check if the direct `bazel_dep` dependencies declared in the root module are the same versions you get in the resolved dependency graph. Valid values are `off` to disable the check, `warning` to print a warning when mismatch detected or `error` to escalate it to a resolution failure.

flags.name: check_fileset_dependencies_recursively
flags.deprecationWarning: This flag is a no-op and fileset dependencies are always checked to ensure correctness of builds.

flags.name: check_licenses
flags.doc: Deprecated in favor of `--config=check_licenses`.

flags.name: check_tests_up_to_date
flags.doc: Don't run tests, just check if they are up-to-date.  If all tests results are up-to-date, the testing completes successfully.  If any test needs to be built or executed, an error is reported and the testing fails.  This option implies --check_up_to_date behavior.

flags.name: check_up_to_date
flags.doc: Don't perform the build, just check if it is up-to-date.  If all targets are up-to-date, the build completes successfully.  If any step needs to be executed an error is reported and the build fails.

flags.name: check_visibility
flags.doc: If disabled, visibility errors in target dependencies are demoted to warnings.

flags.name: client_cwd
flags.doc: A system-generated parameter which specifies the client's working directory

flags.name: client_debug
flags.doc: If true, log debug information from the client to stderr. Changing this option will not cause the server to restart.

flags.name: client_env
flags.doc: A system-generated parameter which specifies the client's environment

flags.name: collapse_duplicate_defines
flags.doc: no-op

flags.name: collect_code_coverage
flags.doc:
If specified, Bazel will instrument code (using offline instrumentation where
possible) and will collect coverage information during tests. Only targets that
match `--instrumentation_filter` will be affected. Usually this option should
not be specified directly - `bazel coverage` command should be used instead.

flags.name: color
flags.doc: Use terminal controls to colorize output.

flags.name: combined_report
flags.doc: Specifies desired cumulative coverage report type. At this point only LCOV is supported.

flags.name: command_port
flags.doc: Port to start up the gRPC command server on. If 0, let the kernel choose.

flags.name: command_wait_time
flags.doc: The time in ms a command had to wait on a busy Bazel server process.

flags.name: compilation_mode
flags.doc: Specify the mode the binary will be built in. Values: `fastbuild`, `dbg`, `opt`.

flags.name: compile_one_dependency
flags.doc: Compile a single dependency of the argument files. This is useful for syntax checking source files in IDEs, for example, by rebuilding a single target that depends on the source file to detect errors as early as possible in the edit/build/test cycle. This argument affects the way all non-flag arguments are interpreted; instead of being targets to build they are source filenames.  For each source filename an arbitrary target that depends on it will be built.

flags.name: compiler
flags.doc: The C++ compiler to use for compiling the target.

flags.name: config
flags.doc: Selects additional config sections from the rc files; for every <command>, it also pulls in the options from <command>:<config> if such a section exists; if this section doesn't exist in any .rc file, Blaze fails with an error. The config sections and flag combinations they are equivalent to are located in the tools/*.blazerc config files.

flags.name: configure
flags.doc:
Only fetches repositories marked as `configure` for system-configuration purpose. Only
works when `--enable_bzlmod` is on.

flags.name: conlyopt
flags.doc: Additional option to pass to gcc when compiling C source files.

flags.name: connect_timeout_secs
flags.doc: The amount of time the client waits for each attempt to connect to the server

flags.name: consistent_labels
flags.doc: If enabled, every query command emits labels as if by the Starlark str function applied to a Label instance. This is useful for tools that need to match the output of different query commands and/or labels emitted by rules. If not enabled, output formatters are free to emit apparent repository names (relative to the main repository) instead to make the output more readable.

flags.name: copt
flags.doc: Additional options to pass to gcc.

flags.name: coverage_output_generator
flags.doc:
Location of the binary that is used to postprocess raw coverage reports. This must
be a binary target. Defaults to `@bazel_tools//tools/test:lcov_merger`.

flags.name: coverage_report_generator
flags.doc:
Location of the binary that is used to generate coverage reports. This must
be a binary target. Defaults to `@bazel_tools//tools/test:coverage_report_generator`.

flags.name: coverage_support
flags.doc:
Location of support files that are required on the inputs of every test action
that collects code coverage. Defaults to `//tools/test:coverage_support`.

flags.name: cpu
flags.doc:
Deprecated: this flag is not used internally by Blaze although there are legacy platform
mappings to allow for backwards compatibility. Do not use this flag, instead use
`--platforms` with an appropriate platform definition.

flags.name: credential_helper
flags.doc:
Configures a credential helper conforming to the [Credential Helper Specification][ch-spec]
to use for retrieving authorization credentials for repository
fetching, remote caching and execution, and the build event service.

Credentials supplied by a helper take precedence over credentials supplied by
`--google_default_credentials`, `--google_credentials`, a `.netrc` file, or the
 auth parameter to `repository_ctx.download()` and
`repository_ctx.download_and_extract()`.

May be specified multiple times to set up multiple helpers.

See [Configuring Bazel's Credential Helper - Engflow Blog][ch-example] for instructions.

[ch-spec]: https://github.com/EngFlow/credential-helper-spec
[ch-example]: https://blog.engflow.com/2023/10/09/configuring-bazels-credential-helper/

flags.name: credential_helper_cache_duration
flags.doc: How long to cache credentials for if the credential helper doesn't return an expiration time. Changing the value of this flag clears the cache.

flags.name: credential_helper_timeout
flags.doc:
Configures the timeout for a credential helper.

Credential helpers failing to respond within this timeout will fail the invocation.

flags.name: crosstool_top
flags.doc: No-op flag. Will be removed in a future release.

flags.name: cs_fdo_absolute_path
flags.doc: Use CSFDO profile information to optimize compilation. Specify the absolute path name of the zip file containing the profile file, a raw or an indexed LLVM profile file.

flags.name: cs_fdo_instrument
flags.doc: Generate binaries with context sensitive FDO instrumentation. With Clang/LLVM compiler, it also accepts the directory name under which the raw profile file(s) will be dumped at runtime.

flags.name: cs_fdo_profile
flags.doc: The cs_fdo_profile representing the context sensitive profile to be used for optimization.

flags.name: curses
flags.doc: Use terminal cursor controls to minimize scrolling output.

flags.name: custom_malloc
flags.doc: Specifies a custom malloc implementation. This setting overrides malloc attributes in build rules.

flags.name: cxxopt
flags.doc: Additional option to pass to gcc when compiling C++ source files.

flags.name: cycles
flags.doc: Points out dependency cycles inside the displayed tree.

flags.name: debug_app
flags.doc: Whether to wait for the debugger before starting the app.

flags.name: default_system_javabase
flags.doc: The root of the user's local JDK install, to be used as the default target javabase and as a fall-back host_javabase. This is not the embedded JDK.

flags.name: default_test_resources
flags.doc:
Override the default resources amount for tests. The expected format is
`{resource}={value}`. If a single positive number is specified as `{value}`
it will override the default resources for all test sizes. If 4
comma-separated numbers are specified, they will override the resource
amount for respectively the `small`, `medium`, `large`, `enormous` test sizes.
Values can also be `HOST_RAM`/`HOST_CPU`, optionally followed
by `[-|*]{float}` (eg. `memory=HOST_RAM*.1,HOST_RAM*.2,HOST_RAM*.3,HOST_RAM*.4`).
The default test resources specified by this flag are overridden by explicit
resources specified in tags.

flags.name: default_visibility
flags.doc: Default visibility for packages that don't set it explicitly ('public' or 'private').

flags.name: defer_param_files
flags.doc: This option is deprecated and has no effect and will be removed in the future.

flags.name: define
flags.doc:
Each `--define` option specifies an assignment for a build variable.
In case of multiple values for a variable, the last one wins.

flags.name: deleted_packages
flags.doc:
A comma-separated list of names of packages which the build system will consider non-existent, even if they are visible somewhere on the package path.
Use this option when deleting a subpackage 'x/y' of an existing package 'x'.  For example, after deleting x/y/BUILD in your client, the build system may complain if it encounters a label '//x:y/z' if that is still provided by another package_path entry.  Specifying --deleted_packages x/y avoids this problem.

flags.name: depth
flags.doc:
Maximum display depth of the dependency tree. A depth of 1 displays the direct
dependencies, for example. For `tree`, `path` and `all_paths` it defaults to
`Integer.MAX_VALUE`, while for `deps` and `explain` it defaults to 1 (only displays
direct deps of the root besides the target leaves and their parents).

flags.name: desugar_for_android
flags.doc: Whether to desugar Java 8 bytecode before dexing.

flags.name: desugar_java8_libs
flags.doc: Whether to include supported Java 8 libraries in apps for legacy devices.

flags.name: device
flags.doc: The adb device serial number. If not specified, the first device will be used.

flags.name: device_debug_entitlements
flags.doc: If set, and compilation mode is not 'opt', objc apps will include debug entitlements when signing.

flags.name: dexopts_supported_in_dexmerger
flags.doc: dx flags supported in tool that merges dex archives into final classes.dex files.

flags.name: dexopts_supported_in_dexsharder
flags.doc: dx flags supported in tool that groups classes for inclusion in final .dex files.

flags.name: dexopts_supported_in_incremental_dexing
flags.doc: dx flags supported when converting Jars to dex archives incrementally.

flags.name: digest_function
flags.doc: The hash function to use when computing file digests.

flags.name: directory_creation_cache
flags.doc: Describes the cache used to store known regular directories as they're created. Parent directories of output files are created on-demand during action execution.

flags.name: disallow_strict_deps_for_jpl
flags.doc: No-op

flags.name: discard_actions_after_execution
flags.doc: This option is deprecated and has no effect.

flags.name: discard_analysis_cache
flags.doc: Discard the analysis cache immediately after the analysis phase completes. Reduces memory usage by ~10%, but makes further incremental builds slower.

flags.name: disk_cache
flags.doc: A path to a directory where Bazel can read and write actions and action outputs. If the directory does not exist, it will be created.

flags.name: distdir
flags.doc: Additional places to search for archives before accessing the network to download them.

flags.name: downloader_config
flags.doc: Specify a file to configure the remote downloader with. This file consists of lines, each of which starts with a directive (`allow`, `block` or `rewrite`) followed by either a host name (for `allow` and `block`) or two patterns, one to match against, and one to use as a substitute URL, with back-references starting from `$1`. It is possible for multiple `rewrite` directives for the same URL to be given, and in this case multiple URLs will be returned.

flags.name: dump_all
flags.doc: If set, dump all known configurations instead of just the ids.

flags.name: dynamic_local_execution_delay
flags.doc: How many milliseconds should local execution be delayed, if remote execution was faster during a build at least once?

flags.name: dynamic_local_strategy
flags.doc: The local strategies, in order, to use for the given mnemonic - the first applicable strategy is used. For example, `worker,sandboxed` runs actions that support persistent workers using the worker strategy, and all others using the sandboxed strategy. If no mnemonic is given, the list of strategies is used as the fallback for all mnemonics. The default fallback list is `worker,sandboxed`, or`worker,sandboxed,standalone` if `experimental_local_lockfree_output` is set. Takes [mnemonic=]local_strategy[,local_strategy,...]

flags.name: dynamic_mode
flags.doc: Determines whether C++ binaries will be linked dynamically.  'default' means Bazel will choose whether to link dynamically.  'fully' means all libraries will be linked dynamically. 'off' means that all libraries will be linked in mostly static mode.

flags.name: dynamic_remote_strategy
flags.doc: The remote strategies, in order, to use for the given mnemonic - the first applicable strategy is used. If no mnemonic is given, the list of strategies is used as the fallback for all mnemonics. The default fallback list is `remote`, so this flag usually does not need to be set explicitly. Takes [mnemonic=]remote_strategy[,remote_strategy,...]

flags.name: emacs
flags.doc: A system-generated parameter which is true iff EMACS=t or INSIDE_EMACS is set in the environment of the client.  This option controls certain display features.

flags.name: embed_label
flags.doc: Embed source control revision or release label in binary

flags.name: emit_script_path_in_exec_request
flags.doc: If true, emits the ExecRequest with --script_path file value and script contents instead of writing the script.

flags.name: enable_bzlmod
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: enable_fdo_profile_absolute_path
flags.doc: Deprecated. No-op.

flags.name: enable_platform_specific_config
flags.doc: If true, Bazel picks up host-OS-specific config lines from bazelrc files. For example, if the host OS is Linux and you run bazel build, Bazel picks up lines starting with build:linux. Supported OS identifiers are linux, macos, windows, freebsd, and openbsd. Enabling this flag is equivalent to using --config=linux on Linux, --config=windows on Windows, etc.

flags.name: enable_propeller_optimize_absolute_paths
flags.doc: If set, any use of absolute paths for propeller optimize will raise an error.

flags.name: enable_remaining_fdo_absolute_paths
flags.doc: If set, any use of absolute paths for FDO will raise an error.

flags.name: enable_runfiles
flags.doc: Enable runfiles symlink tree; By default, it's off on Windows, on on other platforms.

flags.name: enable_workspace
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: enforce_constraints
flags.doc: Checks the environments each target is compatible with and reports errors if any target has dependencies that don't support the same environments

flags.name: enforce_proguard_file_extension
flags.doc: If enabled, requires that ProGuard configuration files outside of third_party/ use the *.pgcfg file extension.

flags.name: enforce_project_configs
flags.doc: If true, interactive builds may only pass the --scl_config build flag; they may not use any other build flags. --scl_config must be set to an officially suported project configuration. Supported configurations are defined in the target's PROJECT.scl, which can be found by walking up the target's packagge path. See b/324126745.

flags.name: exec_aspects
flags.doc: Comma-separated list of aspects to be applied to exec-configured targets, regardless of whether or not they are top-level targets. This is an experimental feature and is subject to change.

flags.name: execution_log_binary_file
flags.doc: Log the executed spawns into this file as length-delimited SpawnExec protos, according to src/main/protobuf/spawn.proto. Prefer --execution_log_compact_file, which is significantly smaller and cheaper to produce. Related flags: --execution_log_compact_file (compact format; mutually exclusive), --execution_log_json_file (text JSON format; mutually exclusive), --execution_log_sort (whether to sort the execution log), --subcommands (for displaying subcommands in terminal output).

flags.name: execution_log_compact_file
flags.doc: Log the executed spawns into this file as length-delimited ExecLogEntry protos, according to src/main/protobuf/spawn.proto. The entire file is zstd compressed. Related flags: --execution_log_binary_file (binary protobuf format; mutually exclusive), --execution_log_json_file (text JSON format; mutually exclusive), --subcommands (for displaying subcommands in terminal output).

flags.name: execution_log_json_file
flags.doc: Log the executed spawns into this file as newline-delimited JSON representations of SpawnExec protos, according to src/main/protobuf/spawn.proto. Prefer --execution_log_compact_file, which is significantly smaller and cheaper to produce. Related flags: --execution_log_compact_file (compact format; mutually exclusive), --execution_log_binary_file (binary protobuf format; mutually exclusive), --execution_log_sort (whether to sort the execution log), --subcommands (for displaying subcommands in terminal output).

flags.name: execution_log_sort
flags.doc: Whether to sort the execution log, making it easier to compare logs across invocations. Set to false to avoid potentially significant CPU and memory usage at the end of the invocation, at the cost of producing the log in nondeterministic execution order. Only applies to the binary and JSON formats; the compact format is never sorted.

flags.name: expand_test_suites
flags.doc: Expand test_suite targets into their constituent tests before analysis. When this flag is turned on (the default), negative target patterns will apply to the tests belonging to the test suite, otherwise they will not. Turning off this flag is useful when top-level aspects are applied at command line: then they can analyze test_suite targets.

flags.name: experimental_action_cache_gc_idle_delay
flags.doc: How long the server must remain idle before a garbage collection of the action cache is attempted. Ineffectual unless --experimental_action_cache_gc_max_age is nonzero.

flags.name: experimental_action_cache_gc_max_age
flags.doc: If set to a nonzero value, the action cache will be periodically garbage collected to remove entries older than this age. Garbage collection occurs in the background once the server has become idle, as determined by the --experimental_action_cache_gc_idle_delay and --experimental_action_cache_gc_threshold flags.

flags.name: experimental_action_cache_gc_threshold
flags.doc: The percentage of stale action cache entries required for garbage collection to be triggered. Ineffectual unless --experimental_action_cache_gc_max_age is nonzero.

flags.name: experimental_action_listener
flags.doc:
Deprecated in favor of aspects. Use `action_listener` to attach an `extra_action` to
existing build actions.

flags.name: experimental_action_resource_set
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: experimental_active_directories
flags.doc: Active directories for Skyfocus and remote analysis caching. Specify as comma-separated workspace root-relative paths. This is a stateful flag. Defining one persists it for subsequent invocations, until it is redefined with a new set.

flags.name: experimental_add_test_support_to_compile_time_deps
flags.doc: Flag to help transition away from adding test support libraries to the compile-time deps of Java test rules.

flags.name: experimental_allow_android_library_deps_without_srcs
flags.doc: No-op. Kept here for backwards compatibility.

flags.name: experimental_allow_map_directory
flags.doc: If enabled, Bazel allows the use of ctx.actions.map_directory(). This allows for the creation of actions based on the files in a directory through a user defined Starlark function and a template_ctx that supports basic action generation APIs.

flags.name: experimental_allow_project_files
flags.doc: Enable processing of +<file> parameters.

flags.name: experimental_allow_runtime_deps_on_neverlink
flags.doc: No-op

flags.name: experimental_always_filter_duplicate_classes_from_android_test
flags.doc: If enabled and the android_test defines a binary_under_test, the class filterering applied to the test's deploy jar will always filter duplicate classes based solely on matching class and package name, ignoring hash values.

flags.name: experimental_analysis_cache_enable_metadata_queries
flags.doc: A flag to switch on/off inserting and querying the metadata db (b/425247333).

flags.name: experimental_analysis_cache_key_distinguisher_for_testing
flags.doc: An opaque string used as part of the cache key. Should only be used for testing.

flags.name: experimental_analysis_cache_server_checksum_override
flags.doc: If set, Blaze will use this checksum to look up entries in the remote analysis cache and not its own. WARNING: this might result in incorrect behavior. Only for debugging. It's best if the difference between the writer and the reader is only additional logging. In particular, the data structures that are being serialized  and the observable behavior of the serialization machinery must not change.

flags.name: experimental_analysis_cache_service
flags.doc: Locator for the AnalysisCacheService instance.

flags.name: experimental_android_assume_minsdkversion
flags.doc: When enabled, the minSdkVersion is parsed from the merged AndroidManifest and used to instruct Proguard on valid Android build versions.

flags.name: experimental_android_compress_java_resources
flags.doc: Compress Java resources in APKs

flags.name: experimental_android_databinding_v2
flags.doc: Use android databinding v2. This flag is a no-op.

flags.name: experimental_android_library_exports_manifest_default
flags.doc: The default value of the exports_manifest attribute on android_library.

flags.name: experimental_android_resource_cycle_shrinking
flags.doc: Enables more shrinking of code and resources by instructing AAPT2 to emit conditional Proguard keep rules.

flags.name: experimental_android_resource_name_obfuscation
flags.doc: Enables obfuscation of resource names within android_binary APKs.

flags.name: experimental_android_resource_path_shortening
flags.doc: Enables shortening of resource file paths within android_binary APKs.

flags.name: experimental_android_resource_shrinking
flags.doc: Enables resource shrinking for android_binary APKs that use ProGuard.

flags.name: experimental_android_rewrite_dexes_with_rex
flags.doc: use rex tool to rewrite dex files

flags.name: experimental_android_use_parallel_dex2oat
flags.doc: Use dex2oat in parallel to possibly speed up android_test.

flags.name: experimental_announce_profile_path
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: experimental_aquery_dump_after_build_format
flags.doc:
Writes the state of Skyframe (which includes previous invocations on this blaze instance
as well) after a build. Output is streamed remotely unless local output is
requested with `--experimental_aquery_dump_after_build_output_file`.  Does not
honor aquery flags for `--include_*`, but uses the same defaults, except for
`--include_commandline=false`. Possible output formats:
`proto|streamed_proto|textproto|jsonproto`. Using this will disable Skymeld.

flags.name: experimental_aquery_dump_after_build_output_file
flags.doc:
Specify the output file for the aquery dump after a build. Use in conjunction with
`--experimental_aquery_dump_after_build_format`. The path provided is relative to
Bazel's output base, unless it's an absolute path. Using this will disable Skymeld.

flags.name: experimental_async_execution
flags.doc:
If set to true, Bazel is allowed to run action in a virtual thread. The number of
actions in flight is still capped with `--jobs`.

flags.name: experimental_async_execution_max_concurrent_actions
flags.doc:
The number of maximum concurrent actions to run with async execution. If the value is
less than `--jobs`, it is clamped to `--jobs`.

flags.name: experimental_bep_target_summary
flags.doc: Whether to publish `TargetSummary` events.

flags.name: experimental_build_event_expand_filesets
flags.doc: If true, expand Filesets in the BEP when presenting output files.

flags.name: experimental_build_event_output_group_mode
flags.doc:
Specify how an output group's files will be represented in `TargetComplete`/`AspectComplete`
BEP events. Values are an assignment of an output group name to one of
`NAMED_SET_OF_FILES_ONLY`, `INLINE_ONLY`, or `BOTH`. The default value is
`NAMED_SET_OF_FILES_ONLY`. If an output group is repeated, the final value to
appear is used. The default value sets the mode for coverage artifacts to BOTH:
`--experimental_build_event_output_group_mode=baseline.lcov=both`

flags.name: experimental_build_event_upload_retry_minimum_delay
flags.doc: Initial, minimum delay for exponential backoff retries when BEP upload fails. (exponent: 1.6)

flags.name: experimental_build_event_upload_strategy
flags.doc:
Selects how to upload artifacts referenced in the build event protocol. In Bazel
the valid options include `local` and `remote`. The default value is `local`.

flags.name: experimental_build_transitive_python_runfiles
flags.doc: No-op

flags.name: experimental_builtins_bzl_path
flags.doc: This flag tells Bazel how to find the "@_builtins" .bzl files that govern how predeclared symbols for BUILD and .bzl files are defined. This flag is only intended for Bazel developers, to help when writing @_builtins .bzl code. Ordinarily this value is set to "%bundled%", which means to use the builtins_bzl/ directory packaged in the Bazel binary. However, it can be set to the path (relative to the root of the current workspace) of an alternate builtins_bzl/ directory, such as one in a Bazel source tree workspace. A literal value of "%workspace%" is equivalent to the relative package path of builtins_bzl/ within a Bazel source tree; this should only be used when running Bazel within its own source tree. Finally, a value of the empty string disables the builtins injection mechanism entirely.

flags.name: experimental_builtins_dummy
flags.doc: Enables an internal dummy symbol used to test builtins injection.

flags.name: experimental_builtins_injection_override
flags.doc: A comma-separated list of symbol names prefixed by a + or - character, indicating which symbols from `@_builtins//:exports.bzl` to inject, overriding their default injection status. Precisely, this works as follows. Each dict key of `exported_toplevels` or `exported_rules` has the form `foo`, `+foo`, or `-foo`. The first two forms mean it gets injected by default, while the last form means it does not get injected by default. In the first case (unprefixed), the default is absolute and cannot be overridden. Otherwise, we then consult this options list, and if we see foo occur here, we take the prefix of its last occurrence and use that to decide whether or not to inject. It is a no-op to specify an unknown symbol, or to attempt to not inject a symbol that occurs unprefixed in a dict key.

flags.name: experimental_bzl_visibility
flags.doc: If enabled, adds a `visibility()` function that .bzl files may call during top-level evaluation to set their visibility for the purpose of load() statements.

flags.name: experimental_cancel_concurrent_tests
flags.doc:
If `on_failed` or `on_passed`, then Blaze will cancel concurrently running tests on the first
successful run with that result. This is only useful in combination with
`--runs_per_test_detects_flakes`.

flags.name: experimental_cc_implementation_deps
flags.doc: If enabled, cc_library targets can use attribute `implementation_deps`.

flags.name: experimental_cc_shared_library
flags.doc: If set to true, rule attributes and Starlark API methods needed for the rule cc_shared_library will be available

flags.name: experimental_cc_skylark_api_enabled_packages
flags.doc: Passes list of packages that can use the C++ Starlark API. Don't enable this flag yet, we will be making breaking changes.

flags.name: experimental_cc_static_library
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: experimental_cgroup_parent
flags.doc: The cgroup where to start the bazel server as an absolute path. The server process will be started in the specified cgroup for each supported controller. For example, if the value of this flag is /build/bazel and the cpu and memory controllers are mounted respectively on /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu and /sys/fs/cgroup/memory, the server will be started in the cgroups /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/build/bazel and /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/build/bazel.It is not an error if the specified cgroup is not writable for one or more of the controllers. This options does not have any effect on platforms that do not support cgroups.

flags.name: experimental_check_desugar_deps
flags.doc: Whether to double-check correct desugaring at Android binary level.

flags.name: experimental_check_external_other_files
flags.doc: Check for modifications made to the non-output, non-repo external files, e.g. host files.

flags.name: experimental_check_external_repository_files
flags.doc: Check for modifications to files in external repositories. Consider setting this flag to false if you don't expect these files to change outside of bazel since it will speed up subsequent runs as they won't have to check a previous run's cache.

flags.name: experimental_check_output_files
flags.doc: Check for modifications made to the output files of a build. Consider setting this flag to false if you don't expect these files to change outside of bazel since it will speed up subsequent runs as they won't have to check a previous run's cache.

flags.name: experimental_circuit_breaker_strategy
flags.doc: Specifies the strategy for the circuit breaker to use. Available strategies are "failure". On invalid value for the option the behavior same as the option is not set.

flags.name: experimental_collect_code_coverage_for_generated_files
flags.doc: If specified, Bazel will also generate collect coverage information for generated files.

flags.name: experimental_collect_load_average_in_profiler
flags.doc: If enabled, the profiler collects the system's overall load average.

flags.name: experimental_collect_local_action_metrics
flags.doc: Deprecated no-op.

flags.name: experimental_collect_local_sandbox_action_metrics
flags.doc: Deprecated no-op.

flags.name: experimental_collect_pressure_stall_indicators
flags.doc: If enabled, the profiler collects the Linux PSI data.

flags.name: experimental_collect_resource_estimation
flags.doc: If enabled, the profiler collects CPU and memory usage estimation for local actions.

flags.name: experimental_collect_skyframe_counts_in_profiler
flags.doc: If enabled, the profiler collects SkyFunction counts in the Skyframe graph over time for key function types, like configured targets and action executions. May have a performance hit as this visits the ENTIRE Skyframe graph at every profiling time unit. Do not use this flag with performance-critical measurements.

flags.name: experimental_collect_system_network_usage
flags.doc: If enabled, the profiler collects the system's network usage.

flags.name: experimental_collect_worker_data_in_profiler
flags.doc: If enabled, the profiler collects worker's aggregated resource data.

flags.name: experimental_command_profile
flags.doc: Records a Java Flight Recorder profile for the duration of the command. One of the supported profiling event types (cpu, wall, alloc or lock) must be given as an argument. The profile is written to a file named after the event type under the output base directory. The syntax and semantics of this flag might change in the future to support additional profile types or output formats; use at your own risk.

flags.name: experimental_convenience_symlinks
flags.doc:
This flag controls how the convenience symlinks (the symlinks that appear in the
workspace after the build) will be managed. Possible values:
- `normal` (default): Each kind of convenience symlink will be created or deleted,
  as determined by the build.
- `clean`: All symlinks will be unconditionally deleted.
- `ignore`: Symlinks will not be created or cleaned up.
- `log_only`: Generate log messages as if `normal` were passed, but don't actually
  perform any filesystem operations (useful for tools).

Note that only symlinks whose names are generated by the current value of
`--symlink_prefix` can be affected; if the prefix changes, any pre-existing
symlinks will be left alone.

flags.name: experimental_convenience_symlinks_bep_event
flags.doc:
This flag controls whether or not we will post the build event
`ConvenienceSymlinksIdentified` to the Build Event Protocol. If the value is true,
the BEP will have an entry for `convenienceSymlinksIdentified`,
listing all of the convenience symlinks created in your workspace. If false, then
the `convenienceSymlinksIdentified` entry in the BEP will be empty.

flags.name: experimental_cpp_compile_resource_estimation
flags.doc: If enabled, will estimate precise resource usage for local execution of CppCompileAction.

flags.name: experimental_cpp_modules
flags.doc: Enables experimental C++20 modules support. Use it with `module_interfaces` attribute on `cc_binary` and `cc_library`. While the support is behind the experimental flag, there are no guarantees about incompatible changes to it or even keeping the support in the future. Consider those risks when using it.

flags.name: experimental_cpu_load_scheduling
flags.doc: Enables the experimental local execution scheduling based on CPU load, not estimation of actions one by one.  Experimental scheduling have showed the large benefit on a large local builds on a powerful machines with the large number of cores. Reccommended to use with --local_resources=cpu=HOST_CPUS

flags.name: experimental_cpu_load_scheduling_window_size
flags.doc: The size of window during experimental scheduling of action based on CPU load. Make sense to define only when flag --experimental_cpu_load_scheduling is enabled.

flags.name: experimental_debug_selects_always_succeed
flags.doc:
When set, `select` functions with no matching clause will return an empty value, instead
of failing. This is to help use `cquery` diagnose failures in `select`.

flags.name: experimental_disable_external_package
flags.doc: If set to true, the auto-generated //external package will not be available anymore. Bazel will still be unable to parse the file 'external/BUILD', but globs reaching into external/ from the unnamed package will work.

flags.name: experimental_disable_instrumentation_manifest_merge
flags.doc: Disables manifest merging when an android_binary has instruments set (i.e. is used for instrumentation testing).

flags.name: experimental_disallow_legacy_java_toolchain_flags
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: experimental_disk_cache_gc_idle_delay
flags.doc: How long the server must remain idle before a garbage collection of the disk cache occurs. To specify the garbage collection policy, set --experimental_disk_cache_gc_max_size and/or --experimental_disk_cache_gc_max_age.

flags.name: experimental_disk_cache_gc_max_age
flags.doc: If set to a positive value, the disk cache will be periodically garbage collected to remove entries older than this age. If set in conjunction with --experimental_disk_cache_gc_max_size, both criteria are applied. Garbage collection occurrs in the background once the server has become idle, as determined by the --experimental_disk_cache_gc_idle_delay flag.

flags.name: experimental_disk_cache_gc_max_size
flags.doc: If set to a positive value, the disk cache will be periodically garbage collected to stay under this size. If set in conjunction with --experimental_disk_cache_gc_max_age, both criteria are applied. Garbage collection occurrs in the background once the server has become idle, as determined by the --experimental_disk_cache_gc_idle_delay flag.

flags.name: experimental_docker_image
flags.doc: Specify a Docker image name (e.g. "ubuntu:latest") that should be used to execute a sandboxed action when using the docker strategy and the action itself doesn't already have a container-image attribute in its remote_execution_properties in the platform description. The value of this flag is passed verbatim to 'docker run', so it supports the same syntax and mechanisms as Docker itself.

flags.name: experimental_docker_privileged
flags.doc: If enabled, Bazel will pass the --privileged flag to 'docker run' when running actions. This might be required by your build, but it might also result in reduced hermeticity.

flags.name: experimental_docker_use_customized_images
flags.doc: If enabled, injects the uid and gid of the current user into the Docker image before using it. This is required if your build / tests depend on the user having a name and home directory inside the container. This is on by default, but you can disable it in case the automatic image customization feature doesn't work in your case or you know that you don't need it.

flags.name: experimental_docker_verbose
flags.doc: If enabled, Bazel will print more verbose messages about the Docker sandbox strategy.

flags.name: experimental_dormant_deps
flags.doc: If set to true, attr.label(materializer=), attr(for_dependency_resolution=), attr.dormant_label(), attr.dormant_label_list() and rule(for_dependency_resolution=) are allowed.

flags.name: experimental_dynamic_exclude_tools
flags.doc: When set, targets that are build "for tool" are not subject to dynamic execution. Such targets are extremely unlikely to be built incrementally and thus not worth spending local cycles on.

flags.name: experimental_dynamic_ignore_local_signals
flags.doc: Takes a list of OS signal numbers. If a local branch of dynamic execution gets killed with any of these signals, the remote branch will be allowed to finish instead. For persistent workers, this only affects signals that kill the worker process.

flags.name: experimental_dynamic_local_load_factor
flags.doc:
Controls how much load from dynamic execution to put on the local machine. This flag adjusts how many actions in dynamic execution we will schedule concurrently. It is based on the number of CPUs Blaze thinks is available, which can be controlled with the --local_resources=cpu= flag.
If this flag is 0, all actions are scheduled locally immediately. If > 0, the amount of actions scheduled locally is limited by the number of CPUs available. If < 1, the load factor is used to reduce the number of locally scheduled actions when the number of actions waiting to schedule is high. This lessens the load on the local machine in the clean build case, where the local machine does not contribute much.

flags.name: experimental_dynamic_slow_remote_time
flags.doc: If >0, the time a dynamically run action must run remote-only before we prioritize its local execution to avoid remote timeouts. This may hide some problems on the remote execution system. Do not turn this on without monitoring of remote execution issues.

flags.name: experimental_enable_android_migration_apis
flags.doc: If set to true, enables the APIs required to support the Android Starlark migration.

flags.name: experimental_enable_critical_path_profiling
flags.doc: If set (the default), critical path profiling is enabled for the execution phase. This has a slight overhead in RAM and CPU, and may prevent Bazel from making certain aggressive RAM optimizations in some cases.

flags.name: experimental_enable_docker_sandbox
flags.doc: Enable Docker-based sandboxing. This option has no effect if Docker is not installed.

flags.name: experimental_enable_execution_graph_log
flags.doc: Enabling this flag makes Blaze write a file of all actions executed during a build. Note that this dump may use a different granularity of actions than other APIs, and may also contain additional information as necessary to reconstruct the full dependency graph in combination with other sources of data.

flags.name: experimental_enable_first_class_macros
flags.doc: If set to true, enables the `macro()` construct for defining symbolic macros.

flags.name: experimental_enable_jspecify
flags.doc: Enable experimental jspecify integration.

flags.name: experimental_enable_scl_dialect
flags.doc: If set to true, .scl files may be used in load() statements.

flags.name: experimental_enable_skyfocus
flags.doc: If true, enable the use of --experimental_active_directories to reduce Bazel's memory footprint for incremental builds. This feature is known as Skyfocus.

flags.name: experimental_enable_starlark_doc_extract
flags.doc: Deprecated no-op.

flags.name: experimental_enable_starlark_set
flags.doc: If true, enable the set data type and set() constructor in Starlark.

flags.name: experimental_enable_thread_dump
flags.doc: Whether to enable thread dumps. If true, Bazel will dump the state of all threads (including virtual threads) to a file every --experimental_thread_dump_interval, or after action execution being inactive for --experimental_thread_dump_action_execution_inactivity_duration. The dumps will be written to the <output_base>/server/thread_dumps/ directory.

flags.name: experimental_enforce_transitive_visibility
flags.doc: If true, enable package()s to set the transitive_visibility attribute to restrict which packages may depend on them.

flags.name: experimental_exclude_defines_from_exec_config
flags.doc:
If true, don't propagate `--define`s to the exec transition at default; only propagate
defines specified by `--experimental_propagate_custom_flag`.

flags.name: experimental_exec_config
flags.doc:
If set to `//some:label:my.bzl%my_transition`, uses my_transition for `cfg = "exec"`
semantics instead of Bazel's internal exec transition logic. Else uses Bazel's
internal logic.

flags.name: experimental_exec_configuration_distinguisher
flags.doc:
Please only use this flag as part of a suggested migration or testing strategy due to
potential for action conflicts. Controls how the execution transition changes the
`--platform_suffix` flag. In `legacy` mode, sets it to a hash of the execution
platform. In `fullhash` mode, sets it to a hash of the entire configuration. In `off`
mode, does not touch it.

flags.name: experimental_execution_graph_enable_edges_from_filewrite_actions
flags.doc: Handle edges from filewrite actions to their inputs correctly.

flags.name: experimental_execution_graph_include_change_pruned_actions
flags.doc: Whether to include change pruned actions in execution graph.

flags.name: experimental_execution_graph_log_dep_type
flags.doc: Selects what kind of dependency information is reported in the action dump. If 'all', every inter-action edge will be reported.

flags.name: experimental_execution_graph_log_path
flags.doc: Local path at which the execution path will be written. If this is set, the log will only be written locally, and not to BEP. If this is set when experimental_enable_execution_graph_log is disabled, there will be an error. If this is unset while BEP uploads are disabled and experimental_enable_execution_graph_log is enabled, the log will be written to a local default.

flags.name: experimental_execution_graph_log_queue_size
flags.doc: The size of the action dump queue, where actions are kept before writing. Larger sizes will increase peak memory usage, but should decrease queue blocking. -1 means unbounded

flags.name: experimental_explicit_aspects
flags.doc: aquery, cquery: whether to include aspect-generated actions in the output. query: no-op (aspects are always followed).

flags.name: experimental_extended_sanity_checks
flags.doc: Enables internal validation checks to make sure that configured target implementations only access things they should. Causes a performance hit.

flags.name: experimental_extra_action_filter
flags.doc: Deprecated in favor of aspects. Filters set of targets to schedule extra_actions for.

flags.name: experimental_extra_action_top_level_only
flags.doc: Deprecated in favor of aspects. Only schedules extra_actions for top level targets.

flags.name: experimental_fetch_all_coverage_outputs
flags.doc: If true, then Bazel fetches the entire coverage data directory for each test during a coverage run.

flags.name: experimental_filter_library_jar_with_program_jar
flags.doc: Filter the ProGuard ProgramJar to remove any classes also present in the LibraryJar.

flags.name: experimental_filter_r_jars_from_android_test
flags.doc: If enabled, R Jars will be filtered from the test apk built by android_test.

flags.name: experimental_fix_deps_tool
flags.doc: Specifies which tool should be used to resolve missing dependencies.

flags.name: experimental_force_gc_after_build
flags.doc: If true calls System.gc() after a build to try and get a post-gc peak heap measurement.

flags.name: experimental_frontier_violation_check
flags.doc: Strategies to handle potential incorrectness from changes beyond the frontier (i.e. outside the active directories)

flags.name: experimental_frontier_violation_verbose
flags.doc: If true, Bazel will print instructions for fixing Skycache violations

flags.name: experimental_fsvc_threads
flags.doc: The number of threads that are used by the `FileSystemValueChecker`.

flags.name: experimental_generate_llvm_lcov
flags.doc: If true, coverage for clang will generate an LCOV report.

flags.name: experimental_genquery_use_graphless_query
flags.doc: Deprecated. No-op.

flags.name: experimental_get_android_java_resources_from_optimized_jar
flags.doc: Get Java resources from _proguard.jar instead of _deploy.jar in android_binary when bundling the final APK.

flags.name: experimental_google_legacy_api
flags.doc: If set to true, exposes a number of experimental pieces of Starlark build API pertaining to Google legacy code.

flags.name: experimental_graphless_query
flags.doc: If true, uses a Query implementation that does not make a copy of the graph. The new implementation only supports --order_output=no, as well as only a subset of output formatters.

flags.name: experimental_import_deps_checking
flags.doc: No-op

flags.name: experimental_include_default_values
flags.doc: Whether Starlark options set to their default values are included in the output.

flags.name: experimental_include_scanning_parallelism
flags.doc: Configures the size of the thread pool used for include scanning. Takes an integer, or a keyword ("auto", "HOST_CPUS", "HOST_RAM"), optionally followed by an operation ([-|*]<float>) eg. "auto", "HOST_CPUS*.5". 0 means to disable parallelism and to just rely on the build graph parallelism for concurrency.  "auto" means to use a reasonable value derived from the machine's hardware profile (e.g. the number of processors).

flags.name: experimental_include_xcode_execution_requirements
flags.doc: If set, add a "requires-xcode:{version}" execution requirement to every Xcode action.  If the Xcode version has a hyphenated label,  also add a "requires-xcode-label:{version_label}" execution requirement.

flags.name: experimental_incremental_dexing_after_proguard
flags.doc: Whether to use incremental dexing tools when building proguarded Android binaries.  Values > 0 turn the feature on, values > 1 run that many dexbuilder shards.

flags.name: experimental_incremental_dexing_after_proguard_by_default
flags.doc: Whether to use incremental dexing for proguarded Android binaries by default.  Use incremental_dexing attribute to override default for a particular android_binary.

flags.name: experimental_inmemory_dotd_files
flags.doc: If enabled, C++ .d files will be passed through in memory directly from the remote build nodes instead of being written to disk.

flags.name: experimental_inmemory_dotincludes_files
flags.doc: If enabled, searching for '#include' lines in generated header files will not touch local disk. This makes include scanning of C++ files less disk-intensive.

flags.name: experimental_inmemory_jdeps_files
flags.doc: If enabled, the dependency (.jdeps) files generated from Java compilations will be passed through in memory directly from the remote build nodes instead of being written to disk.

flags.name: experimental_inmemory_sandbox_stashes
flags.doc: If set to true, the contents of stashed sandboxes for reuse_sandbox_directories will be tracked in memory. This reduces the amount of I/O needed during reuse. Depending on the build this flag may improve wall time. Depending on the build as well this flag may use a significant amount of additional memory.

flags.name: experimental_install_base_gc_max_age
flags.doc: How long an install base must go unused before it's eligible for garbage collection. If nonzero, the server will attempt to garbage collect other install bases when idle.

flags.name: experimental_isolated_extension_usages
flags.doc: If true, enables the isolate parameter in the use_extension function.

flags.name: experimental_java_classpath
flags.doc: Enables reduced classpaths for Java compilations.

flags.name: experimental_java_header_compilation_direct_deps
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: experimental_java_header_input_pruning
flags.doc: No-op

flags.name: experimental_java_proto_add_allowed_public_imports
flags.doc: This flag is a noop and scheduled for removal.

flags.name: experimental_java_test_auto_create_deploy_jar
flags.doc: DO NOT USE

flags.name: experimental_lazy_macro_expansion_packages
flags.doc: List of packages in which symbolic macro are expanded only if necessary.

flags.name: experimental_limit_android_lint_to_android_constrained_java
flags.doc: No-op

flags.name: experimental_link_static_libraries_once
flags.doc: If enabled, cc_shared_library will link all libraries statically linked into it, that should only be linked once.

flags.name: experimental_local_java_optimization_configuration
flags.doc: Do not use.

flags.name: experimental_local_java_optimizations
flags.doc: Do not use.

flags.name: experimental_local_lockfree_output
flags.doc: When true, the local spawn runner doesn't lock the output tree during dynamic execution. Instead, spawns are allowed to execute until they are explicitly interrupted by a faster remote action.

flags.name: experimental_local_retries_on_crash
flags.doc: Number of times to retry a local action when we detect that it crashed. This exists to workaround a bug in OSXFUSE which is tickled by the use of the dynamic scheduler and --experimental_local_lockfree_output due to constant process churn. The bug can be triggered by a cancelled process that ran *before* the process we are trying to run, introducing corruption in its file reads.

flags.name: experimental_materialize_param_files_directly
flags.doc: If materializing param files, do so with direct writes to disk.

flags.name: experimental_max_directories_to_eagerly_visit_in_globbing
flags.doc: If non-negative, the first time a glob is evaluated in a package, the subdirectories of the package will be traversed in order to warm filesystem caches and compensate for lack of parallelism in globbing. At most this many directories will be visited.

flags.name: experimental_merged_skyframe_analysis_execution
flags.doc: If this flag is set, the analysis and execution phases of Skyframe are merged.

flags.name: experimental_objc_fastbuild_options
flags.doc: Uses these strings as objc fastbuild compiler options.

flags.name: experimental_objc_provider_from_linked
flags.doc: No-op. Kept here for backwards compatibility. This field will be removed in a future release.

flags.name: experimental_omit_resources_info_provider_from_android_binary
flags.doc: Omit AndroidResourcesInfo provider from android_binary rules. Propagating resources out to other binaries is usually unintentional.

flags.name: experimental_omitfp
flags.doc: If true, use libunwind for stack unwinding, and compile with -fomit-frame-pointer and -fasynchronous-unwind-tables.

flags.name: experimental_one_version_enforcement
flags.doc: When enabled, enforce that a java_binary rule can't contain more than one version of the same class file on the classpath. This enforcement can break the build, or can just result in warnings.

flags.name: experimental_one_version_enforcement_use_transitive_jars_for_binary_under_test
flags.doc: If enabled, one version enforcement for android_test uses the binary_under_test's transitive classpath, otherwise it uses the deploy jar

flags.name: experimental_oom_sensitive_skyfunctions_semaphore_size
flags.doc: Sets the size of the semaphore used to prevent SkyFunctions with large peak memory requirement from OOM-ing blaze. A value of 0 indicates that no semaphore should be used. Example value: `HOST_CPUS*0.5`.

flags.name: experimental_output_directory_naming_scheme
flags.doc:
Please only use this flag as part of a suggested migration or testing strategy. In
`legacy` mode, transitions (generally only Starlark) set and use `affected by Starlark transition`
