to determine the ST hash. In `diff_against_baseline` mode,
`affected by Starlark transition` is ignored and instead ST hash is determined,
for all configuration, by diffing against the top-level configuration.

flags.name: experimental_output_paths
flags.doc:
Which model to use for where in the output tree rules write their outputs, particularly
for multi-platform / multi-configuration builds. This is highly experimental. See
[GH-6526] for details. Starlark actions can opt into path mapping by adding the key
`supports-path-mapping` to the `execution_requirements` dict.

[GH-6526]: https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/6526

flags.name: experimental_override_platform_cpu_name
flags.doc:
Each entry should be of the form `label=value` where label refers to a platform and values
is the desired shortname to override the platform's CPU name in `$(TARGET_CPU)`
make variable and output path. Only used when
`--experimental_platform_in_output_dir`, `--incompatible_target_cpu_from_platform` or
`--incompatible_bep_cpu_from_platform` is true. Has highest naming priority.

flags.name: experimental_parallel_aquery_output
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: experimental_parse_headers_skipped_if_corresponding_srcs_found
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: experimental_persistent_aar_extractor
flags.doc: Enable persistent aar extractor by using workers.

flags.name: experimental_platform_cc_test
flags.doc: Deprecated. No-op.

flags.name: experimental_platform_in_output_dir
flags.doc:
If true, a shortname for the target platform is used in the output directory name
instead of the CPU. The exact scheme is experimental and subject to change:
1. First, in the rare case the `--platforms` option does not have exactly one value, a
   hash of the platforms option is used.
2. Next, if any shortname for the current platform was registered by
   `--experimental_override_name_platform_in_output_dir`, then that shortname is used.
3. Then, if `--experimental_use_platforms_in_output_dir_legacy_heuristic` is set, use a
   shortname based off the current platform Label.
4. Finally, a hash of the platform option is used as a last resort.

flags.name: experimental_platforms_api
flags.doc: If set to true, enables a number of platform-related Starlark APIs useful for debugging.

flags.name: experimental_post_profile_started_event
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: experimental_prefer_mutual_xcode
flags.doc: If true, use the most recent Xcode that is available both locally and remotely. If false, or if there are no mutual available versions, use the local Xcode version selected via xcode-select.

flags.name: experimental_process_wrapper_graceful_sigterm
flags.doc: When true, make the process-wrapper propagate SIGTERMs (used by the dynamic scheduler to stop process trees) to the subprocesses themselves, giving them the grace period in --local_termination_grace_seconds before forcibly sending a SIGKILL.

flags.name: experimental_profile_action_counts
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: experimental_profile_additional_tasks
flags.doc: Specifies additional profile tasks to be included in the profile.

flags.name: experimental_profile_include_primary_output
flags.doc: Includes the extra "out" attribute in action events that contains the exec path to the action's primary output.

flags.name: experimental_profile_include_target_configuration
flags.doc: Includes target configuration hash in action events' JSON profile data.

flags.name: experimental_profile_include_target_label
flags.doc: Includes target label in action events' JSON profile data.

flags.name: experimental_propagate_custom_flag
flags.doc:
Which custom flags (starlark flags or defines) to propagate to the exec transition, by
key. e.g. if `--define=a=b` should be propagated, set
`--experimental_propagate_custom_flag=a`

flags.name: experimental_proto_descriptor_sets_include_source_info
flags.doc: Run extra actions for alternative Java api versions in a proto_library.

flags.name: experimental_proto_extra_actions
flags.doc: Deprecated. No-op.

flags.name: experimental_publish_package_metrics_in_bep
flags.doc: Whether to publish package metrics in the BEP.

flags.name: experimental_py_binaries_include_label
flags.doc: py_binary targets include their label even when stamping is disabled.

flags.name: experimental_python_import_all_repositories
flags.doc:
If true, the roots of repositories in the runfiles tree are added to `PYTHONPATH`, so
that imports like `import mytoplevelpackage.package.module` are valid.
Regardless of whether this flag is true, the runfiles root itself is also
added to the `PYTHONPATH`, so
`import myreponame.mytoplevelpackage.package.module` is valid. The latter form
is less likely to experience import name collisions.

flags.name: experimental_record_metrics_for_all_mnemonics
flags.doc: Controls the output of BEP ActionSummary and BuildGraphMetrics, limiting the number of mnemonics in ActionData and number of entries reported in BuildGraphMetrics.AspectCount/RuleClassCount. By default the number of types is limited to the top 20, by number of executed actions for ActionData, and instances for RuleClass and Asepcts. Setting this option will write statistics for all mnemonics, rule classes and aspects.

flags.name: experimental_record_skyframe_metrics
flags.doc: Controls the output of BEP BuildGraphMetrics, including expensiveto compute skyframe metrics about Skykeys, RuleClasses and Aspects.With this flag set to false BuildGraphMetrics.rule_count and aspectfields will not be populated in the BEP.

flags.name: experimental_remotable_source_manifests
flags.doc: Whether to make source manifest actions remotable

flags.name: experimental_remote_analysis_cache
flags.doc: The URL for the remote analysis caching backend.

flags.name: experimental_remote_analysis_cache_concurrency
flags.doc: Target concurrency for remote analysis caching RPCs.

flags.name: experimental_remote_analysis_cache_deadline
flags.doc: Deadline to use for remote analysis cache operations.

flags.name: experimental_remote_analysis_cache_max_batch_size
flags.doc: Batch size limit for remote analysis caching RPCs.

flags.name: experimental_remote_analysis_cache_mode
flags.doc: The transport direction for the remote analysis cache.

flags.name: experimental_remote_analysis_unreachable_cache_retry_interval
flags.doc: How long to wait before retrying a cache get request that failed due to an UNREACHABLE channel. This is a workaround for the client library reporting 'ready' prematurely.

flags.name: experimental_remote_analysis_write_proxy
flags.doc: The address of the SkycacheStorageWriteProxyService. If set, this service will be used for uploading analysis cache data.

flags.name: experimental_remote_cache_chunking
flags.doc: If enabled, large blobs are split into content-defined chunks and uploaded/downloaded in chunks, enabling deduplication across blobs. The server must advertise SplitBlob/SpliceBlob RPCs and the parameters of the chunking function selected by --experimental_remote_cache_chunking_function in its capabilities.

flags.name: experimental_remote_cache_chunking_function
flags.doc: The content-defined chunking function used to split large blobs when --experimental_remote_cache_chunking is enabled. If set to 'auto' (the default), the function is negotiated with the server: FastCDC 2020 is used if the server advertises it, otherwise RepMaxCDC. Set to 'fast_cdc_2020' or 'rep_max_cdc' to require a specific function, in which case the server must advertise the parameters of that function in its capabilities. All clients sharing a cache should use the same function to maximize chunk reuse.

flags.name: experimental_remote_cache_compression_threshold
flags.doc: The minimum blob size required to compress/decompress with zstd. Ineffectual unless --remote_cache_compression is set.

flags.name: experimental_remote_cache_eviction_retries
flags.doc: The maximum number of attempts to retry if the build encountered a transient remote cache error that would otherwise fail the build. Applies for example when artifacts are evicted from the remote cache, or in certain cache failure conditions. A new invocation id will be generated for each attempt.

flags.name: experimental_remote_cache_lease_extension
flags.doc: If set to true, Bazel will extend the lease for outputs of remote actions during the build by sending `FindMissingBlobs` calls periodically to remote cache. The frequency is based on the value of `--experimental_remote_cache_ttl`.

flags.name: experimental_remote_cache_ttl
flags.doc: The guaranteed minimal TTL of blobs in the remote cache after their digests are recently referenced e.g. by an ActionResult or FindMissingBlobs. Bazel does several optimizations based on the blobs' TTL e.g. doesn't repeatedly call GetActionResult in an incremental build. The value should be set slightly less than the real TTL since there is a gap between when the server returns the digests and when Bazel receives them.

flags.name: experimental_remote_capture_corrupted_outputs
flags.doc: A path to a directory where the corrupted outputs will be captured to.

flags.name: experimental_remote_discard_merkle_trees
flags.doc: If set to true, discard in-memory copies of the input root's Merkle tree and associated input mappings during calls to GetActionResult() and Execute(). This reduces memory usage significantly, but does require Bazel to recompute them upon remote cache misses and retries.

flags.name: experimental_remote_downloader
flags.doc: A Remote Asset API endpoint URI, to be used as a remote download proxy. The supported schemas are grpc, grpcs (grpc with TLS enabled) and unix (local UNIX sockets). If no schema is provided Bazel will default to grpcs. See: https://github.com/bazelbuild/remote-apis/blob/master/build/bazel/remote/asset/v1/remote_asset.proto

flags.name: experimental_remote_downloader_local_fallback
flags.doc: Whether to fall back to the local downloader if remote downloader fails.

flags.name: experimental_remote_downloader_propagate_credentials
flags.doc: Whether to propagate credentials from netrc and credential helper to the remote downloader server. The server implementation needs to support the new `http_header_url:<url-index>:<header-key>` qualifier where the `<url-index>` is a 0-based position of the URL inside the FetchBlobRequest's `uris` field. The URL-specific headers should take precedence over the global headers.

flags.name: experimental_remote_execution_keepalive
flags.doc: No-op. Kept here for backwards compatibility.

flags.name: experimental_remote_failure_rate_threshold
flags.doc: Sets the allowed number of failure rate in percentage for a specific time window after which it stops calling to the remote cache/executor. By default the value is 10. Setting this to 0 means no limitation.

flags.name: experimental_remote_failure_window_interval
flags.doc: The interval in which the failure rate of the remote requests are computed. On zero or negative value the failure duration is computed the whole duration of the execution.Following units can be used: Days (d), hours (h), minutes (m), seconds (s), and milliseconds (ms). If the unit is omitted, the value is interpreted as seconds.

flags.name: experimental_remote_include_extraction_size_threshold
flags.doc: Run remotable C++ include extraction remotely if the file size in bytes exceeds this.

flags.name: experimental_remote_mark_tool_inputs
flags.doc: If set to true, Bazel will mark inputs as tool inputs for the remote executor. This can be used to implement remote persistent workers.

flags.name: experimental_remote_output_service
flags.doc: HOST or HOST:PORT of a remote output service endpoint. The supported schemas are grpc, grpcs (grpc with TLS enabled) and unix (local UNIX sockets). If no schema is provided Bazel will default to grpcs. Specify grpc:// or unix: schema to disable TLS.

flags.name: experimental_remote_output_service_output_path_prefix
flags.doc: The path under which the contents of output directories managed by the --experimental_remote_output_service are placed. The actual output directory used by a build will be a descendant of this path and determined by the output service.

flags.name: experimental_remote_repo_contents_cache
flags.doc:
If enabled, the remote cache will be used to store the results of reproducible repository
rules. If a repository rule needs to be evaluated and its result is already in the remote
cache, the contents of the repository will be kept in an in-memory file system and are
only downloaded when needed, either by Bazel itself or an action that runs locally.

flags.name: experimental_remote_require_cached
flags.doc: If set to true, enforce that all actions that can run remotely are cached, or else fail the build. This is useful to troubleshoot non-determinism issues as it allows checking whether actions that should be cached are actually cached without spuriously injecting new results into the cache.

flags.name: experimental_remote_scrubbing_config
flags.doc:
Enables remote cache key scrubbing with the supplied configuration file, which must be a protocol buffer in text format (see src/main/protobuf/remote_scrubbing.proto).

This feature is intended to facilitate sharing a remote/disk cache between actions executing on different platforms but targeting the same platform. It should be used with extreme care, as improper settings may cause accidental sharing of cache entries and result in incorrect builds.

Scrubbing does not affect how an action is executed, only how its remote/disk cache key is computed for the purpose of retrieving or storing an action result. Scrubbed actions are incompatible with remote execution, and will always be executed locally instead.

Modifying the scrubbing configuration does not invalidate outputs present in the local filesystem or internal caches; a clean build is required to reexecute affected actions.

In order to successfully use this feature, you likely want to set a custom --host_platform together with --experimental_platform_in_output_dir (to normalize output prefixes).

flags.name: experimental_remove_r_classes_from_instrumentation_test_jar
flags.doc: If enabled and the test instruments an application, all the R classes from the test's deploy jar will be removed.

flags.name: experimental_repo_remote_exec
flags.doc: If set to true, repository_rule gains some remote execution capabilities.

flags.name: experimental_repository_cache_hardlinks
flags.doc: If set, the repository cache will hardlink the file in case of a cache hit, rather than copying. This is intended to save disk space.

flags.name: experimental_repository_ctx_execute_wasm
flags.doc: If true enables the repository_ctx `load_wasm` and `execute_wasm` methods.

flags.name: experimental_repository_downloader_retries
flags.doc: The maximum number of attempts to retry a download error. If set to 0, retries are disabled.

flags.name: experimental_require_availability_info
flags.doc: Deprecated no-op.

flags.name: experimental_retain_test_configuration_across_testonly
flags.doc:
When enabled, `--trim_test_configuration` will not trim the test configuration for rules
marked testonly=1. This is meant to reduce action conflict issues when non-test
rules depend on `cc_test` rules. No effect if `--trim_test_configuration` is
false.

flags.name: experimental_reuse_include_scanning_threads
flags.doc: If enabled core threads of include scanner pool will not die during execution.

flags.name: experimental_rule_extension_api
flags.doc: Enable experimental rule extension API and subrule APIs

flags.name: experimental_run_android_lint_on_java_rules
flags.doc: Whether to validate java_* sources.

flags.name: experimental_run_bep_event_include_residue
flags.doc: Whether to include the command-line residue in run build events which could contain the residue. By default, the residue is not included in run command build events that could contain the residue.

flags.name: experimental_run_in_user_cgroup
flags.doc: If true, the Bazel server will be run with systemd-run, and the user will own the cgroup. This flag only takes effect on Linux.

flags.name: experimental_sandbox_async_tree_delete_idle_threads
flags.doc: If 0, sandboxes are deleted as soon as actions finish, blocking action completion. If greater than 0, sandboxes are deleted asynchronously in the background without blocking action completion. Asynchronous deletion uses a single thread while a command is running, but ramps up to as many threads as the value of this flag once the server becomes idle. Set to `auto` to use as many threads as the number of CPUs. A server shutdown blocks on any pending asynchronous deletions.

flags.name: experimental_sandbox_enforce_resources_regexp
flags.doc: If true, actions whose mnemonic matches the input regex will have their resources request enforced as limits, overriding the value of --experimental_sandbox_limits, if the resource type supports it. For example a test that declares cpu:3 and resources:memory:10, will run with at most 3 cpus and 10 megabytes of memory.

flags.name: experimental_sandbox_limits
flags.doc: If > 0, each Linux sandbox will be limited to the given amount for the specified resource. Requires --incompatible_use_new_cgroup_implementation and overrides --experimental_sandbox_memory_limit_mb. Requires cgroups v1 or v2 and permissions for the users to the cgroups dir.

flags.name: experimental_sandbox_memory_limit_mb
flags.doc: If > 0, each Linux sandbox will be limited to the given amount of memory (in MB). Requires cgroups v1 or v2 and permissions for the users to the cgroups dir.

flags.name: experimental_sandboxfs_map_symlink_targets
flags.doc: No-op

flags.name: experimental_save_feature_state
flags.doc: Save the state of enabled and requested feautres as an output of compilation.

flags.name: experimental_scale_timeouts
flags.doc: Scale all timeouts in Starlark repository rules by this factor. In this way, external repositories can be made working on machines that are slower than the rule author expected, without changing the source code

flags.name: experimental_show_artifacts
flags.doc: Deprecated no-op.

flags.name: experimental_shrink_worker_pool
flags.doc: If enabled, could shrink worker pool if worker memory pressure is high. This flag works only when flag experimental_total_worker_memory_limit_mb is enabled.

flags.name: experimental_sibling_repository_layout
flags.doc: If set to true, non-main repositories are planted as symlinks to the main repository in the execution root. That is, all repositories are direct children of the $output_base/execution_root directory. This has the side effect of freeing up $output_base/execution_root/__main__/external for the real top-level 'external' directory.

flags.name: experimental_single_package_toolchain_binding
flags.doc: If enabled, the register_toolchain function may not include target patterns which may refer to more than one package.

flags.name: experimental_skip_ttvs_for_genquery
flags.doc: No-op. Will be removed soon.

flags.name: experimental_skyfocus_dump_keys
flags.doc: For debugging Skyfocus. Dump the focused SkyKeys (roots, leafs, focused deps, focused rdeps).

flags.name: experimental_skyfocus_dump_post_gc_stats
flags.doc: For debugging Skyfocus. If enabled, trigger manual GC before/after focusing to report heap sizes reductions. This will increase the Skyfocus latency.

flags.name: experimental_skyframe_cpu_heavy_skykeys_thread_pool_size
flags.doc: If set to a positive value (e.g. `HOST_CPUS*1.5`), Skyframe will run the loading/analysis phase with 2 separate thread pools: 1 with `<value>` threads (ideally close to `HOST_CPUS`) reserved for CPU-heavy SkyKeys, and 1 "standard" thread pool (whose size is controlled by `--loading_phase_threads`) for the rest.

flags.name: experimental_skyframe_error_handling_refactor
flags.doc: Used solely for the safe rollout of simplifying Skyframe error handling. This will beremoved once the rollout is complete (expected timeframe: 1 release)

flags.name: experimental_skyframe_memory_dump
flags.doc:
Dump the memory use of individual nodes in the Skyframe graph after the build. This
option takes a number of flags separated by commas:
- `json` (no-op, that's the only format).
- `notransient` (don't traverse transient fields).
- `noconfig` (ignore objects related to configurations).
- `noprecomputed` (ignore precomputed values).
- `noworkspacestatus` (ignore objects related to the workspace status machinery).

flags.name: experimental_skyframe_native_filesets
flags.deprecationWarning: This flag is a no-op and skyframe-native-filesets is always true.

flags.name: experimental_skyframe_prepare_analysis
flags.doc: Deprecated. No-op.
flags.deprecationWarning: This flag is a no-op and will be deleted in a future release.

flags.name: experimental_skyframe_target_pattern_evaluator
flags.doc: Use the Skyframe-based target pattern evaluator; implies --experimental_interleave_loading_and_analysis.

flags.name: experimental_skylark_debug
flags.doc: If true, Blaze will open the Starlark debug server at the start of the build invocation, and wait for a debugger to attach before running the build.

flags.name: experimental_skylark_debug_reset_analysis
flags.doc: If true, resets analysis before executing the build. Has no effect without --experimental_skylark_debug

flags.name: experimental_skylark_debug_server_port
flags.doc: The port on which the Starlark debug server will listen for connections.

flags.name: experimental_skylark_debug_verbose_logging
flags.doc: Show verbose logs for the debugger.

flags.name: experimental_skymeld_analysis_overlap_percentage
flags.doc: The value represents the % of the analysis phase which will be overlapped with the execution phase. A value of x means Skyframe will queue up execution tasks and wait until there's x% of the top level target left to be analyzed before allowing them to launch. When the value is 0%, we'd wait for all analysis to finish before executing (no overlap). When it's 100%, the phases are free to overlap as much as they can.

flags.name: experimental_spawn_scheduler
flags.doc: Enable dynamic execution by running actions locally and remotely in parallel. Bazel spawns each action locally and remotely and picks the one that completes first. If an action supports workers, the local action will be run in the persistent worker mode. To enable dynamic execution for an individual action mnemonic, use the `--internal_spawn_scheduler` and `--strategy=<mnemonic>=dynamic` flags instead.
flags.deprecationWarning: --experimental_spawn_scheduler is deprecated. Using dynamic execution for everything is rarely a good idea (see https://bazel.build/remote/dynamic). If you really want to enable dynamic execution globally, pass `--internal_spawn_scheduler --spawn_strategy=dynamic`.

flags.name: experimental_split_coverage_postprocessing
flags.doc: If true, then Bazel will run coverage postprocessing for test in a new spawn.

flags.name: experimental_starlark_cc_import
flags.doc: Deprecated. No-op.

flags.name: experimental_starlark_type_checking
flags.doc: Enables type checking in files and functions that contain type annotations or related syntax. (When this flag is disabled, Bazel is more forgiving of invalid types in type annotations.)

flags.name: experimental_starlark_type_syntax
flags.doc:
Enables type annotations and related syntax in .bzl files. Locations of files where these are allowed is further restricted by `--experimental_starlark_types_allowed_paths`.
Type syntax is never permitted in .scl files regardless of this flag.

flags.name: experimental_starlark_types
flags.doc: No-op. Previously used as --experimental_starlark_type_syntax + --experimental_starlark_type_checking

flags.name: experimental_starlark_types_allowed_paths
flags.doc: List of canonical Label prefixes under which Starlark type annotations are allowed.

flags.name: experimental_stats_summary
flags.doc: Enable a modernized summary of the build stats.

flags.name: experimental_stream_log_file_uploads
flags.doc: Stream log file uploads directly to the remote storage rather than writing them to disk.

flags.name: experimental_strict_fileset_output
flags.doc: If this option is enabled, filesets will treat all output artifacts as regular files. They will not traverse directories or be sensitive to symlinks.

flags.name: experimental_strict_java_deps
flags.doc: If true, checks that a Java target explicitly declares all directly used targets as dependencies.

flags.name: experimental_strict_repo_env
flags.doc:
If true, repository rules and module extensions will only inherit `PATH`, `PATHEXT`
(on Windows), and environment variables explicitly specified by `--repo_env`.

Note that unless `--incompatible_repo_env_ignores_action_env` is true,
`--action_env=NAME=VALUE` will also be included.

flags.name: experimental_thread_dump_action_execution_inactivity_duration
flags.doc: Dump the threads when action execution being inactive for this duration. If zero, no thread dumps are written for action execution being inactive.

flags.name: experimental_thread_dump_interval
flags.doc: How often to dump the threads periodically. If zero, no thread dumps are written periodically.

flags.name: experimental_throttle_action_cache_check
flags.doc: Whether to throttle the check whether an action is cached.

flags.name: experimental_throttle_remote_action_building
flags.doc:
Whether to throttle the building of remote action to avoid OOM. Defaults to true.

This is a temporary flag to allow users switch off the behaviour. Once Bazel is smart enough about the RAM/CPU usages, this flag will be removed.

flags.name: experimental_tool_command_line
flags.doc: An extra command line to report with this invocation's command line. Useful for tools that invoke Bazel and want the original information that the tool received to be logged with the rest of the Bazel invocation.

flags.name: experimental_total_worker_memory_limit_mb
flags.doc: If this limit is greater than zero idle workers might be killed if the total memory usage of all  workers exceed the limit.

flags.name: experimental_turbine_annotation_processing
flags.doc: If enabled, turbine is used for all annotation processing

flags.name: experimental_ui_debug_all_events
flags.doc: Report all events known to the Bazel UI.

flags.name: experimental_ui_max_stdouterr_bytes
flags.doc: The maximum size of the stdout / stderr files that will be printed to the console. -1 implies no limit.

flags.name: experimental_unsupported_and_brittle_include_scanning
flags.doc: Whether to narrow inputs to C/C++ compilation by parsing #include lines from input files. This can improve performance and incrementality by decreasing the size of compilation input trees. However, it can also break builds because the include scanner does not fully implement C preprocessor semantics. In particular, it does not understand dynamic #include directives and ignores preprocessor conditional logic. Use at your own risk. Any issues relating to this flag that are filed will be closed. At Google without this flag your build will most likely fail.

flags.name: experimental_use_cpp_compile_action_args_params_file
flags.doc: If enabled, write CppCompileAction exposed action.args to parameters file.

flags.name: experimental_use_dex_splitter_for_incremental_dexing
flags.doc: Do not use.

flags.name: experimental_use_event_based_build_completion_status
flags.doc: No-op

flags.name: experimental_use_hermetic_linux_sandbox
flags.doc: If set to true, do not mount root, only mount whats provided with sandbox_add_mount_pair. Input files will be hardlinked to the sandbox instead of symlinked to from the sandbox. If action input files are located on a filesystem different from the sandbox, then the input files will be copied instead.

flags.name: experimental_use_llvm_covmap
flags.doc: If specified, Bazel will generate llvm-cov coverage map information rather than gcov when collect_code_coverage is enabled.

flags.name: experimental_use_new_worker_pool
flags.doc: No-op

flags.name: experimental_use_platforms_in_output_dir_legacy_heuristic
flags.doc:
Please only use this flag as part of a suggested migration or testing strategy. Note
that the heuristic has known deficiencies and it is suggested to migrate to
relying on just `--experimental_override_name_platform_in_output_dir`.

flags.name: experimental_use_rtxt_from_merged_resources
flags.doc: Use R.txt from the merging action, instead of from the validation action.

flags.name: experimental_use_semaphore_for_jobs
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: experimental_use_validation_aspect
flags.doc: Whether to run validation actions using aspect (for parallelism with tests).

flags.name: experimental_use_windows_sandbox
flags.doc: Use Windows sandbox to run actions. If "yes", the binary provided by --experimental_windows_sandbox_path must be valid and correspond to a supported version of sandboxfs. If "auto", the binary may be missing or not compatible.

flags.name: experimental_windows_sandbox_path
flags.doc: Path to the Windows sandbox binary to use when --experimental_use_windows_sandbox is true. If a bare name, use the first binary of that name found in the PATH.

flags.name: experimental_windows_watchfs
flags.doc: If true, experimental Windows support for --watchfs is enabled. Otherwise --watchfsis a non-op on Windows. Make sure to also enable --watchfs.

flags.name: experimental_worker_allowlist
flags.doc: If non-empty, only allow using persistent workers with the given worker key mnemonic.

flags.name: experimental_worker_as_resource
flags.doc: No-op, will be removed soon.

flags.name: experimental_worker_cancellation
flags.doc: If enabled, Bazel may send cancellation requests to workers that support them.

flags.name: experimental_worker_memory_limit_mb
flags.doc: If this limit is greater than zero, workers might be killed if the memory usage of the worker exceeds the limit. If not used together with dynamic execution and `--experimental_dynamic_ignore_local_signals=9`, this may crash your build.

flags.name: experimental_worker_metrics_poll_interval
flags.doc: The interval between collecting worker metrics and possibly attempting evictions. Cannot effectively be less than 1s for performance reasons.

flags.name: experimental_worker_multiplex_sandboxing
flags.doc: If enabled, multiplex workers with a 'supports-multiplex-sandboxing' execution requirement will run in a sandboxed environment, using a separate sandbox directory per work request. Multiplex workers with the execution requirement are always sandboxed when running under the dynamic execution strategy, irrespective of this flag.

flags.name: experimental_worker_sandbox_hardening
flags.doc: If enabled, workers are run in a hardened sandbox, if the implementation allows it. If hardening is enabled then tmp directories are distinct for different workers.

flags.name: experimental_worker_sandbox_inmemory_tracking
flags.doc: A worker key mnemonic for which the contents of the sandbox directory are tracked in memory. This may improve build performance at the cost of additional memory usage. Only affects sandboxed workers. May be specified multiple times for different mnemonics.

flags.name: experimental_worker_strict_flagfiles
flags.doc: If enabled, actions arguments for workers that do not follow the worker specification will cause an error. Worker arguments must have exactly one @flagfile argument as the last of its list of arguments.

flags.name: experimental_worker_use_cgroups_on_linux
flags.doc: On linux, run all workers in its own cgroup (without any limits set) and use the cgroup's own resource accounting for memory measurements. This is overridden by --experimental_worker_sandbox_hardening for sandboxed workers.

flags.name: experimental_workspace_rules_log_file
flags.doc: Log certain Workspace Rules events into this file as delimited WorkspaceEvent protos.

flags.name: experimental_writable_outputs
flags.doc: If true, the file permissions of action outputs are set to `0755` instead of `0555`

flags.name: explain
flags.doc: Causes the build system to explain each executed step of the build. The explanation is written to the specified log file.

flags.name: explicit_java_test_deps
flags.doc: Explicitly specify a dependency to JUnit or Hamcrest in a java_test instead of  accidentally obtaining from the TestRunner's deps. Only works for bazel right now.

flags.name: expunge
flags.doc: If true, clean removes the entire working tree for this %{product} instance, which includes all %{product}-created temporary and build output files, and stops the %{product} server if it is running.

flags.name: expunge_async
flags.doc: If specified, clean asynchronously removes the entire working tree for this %{product} instance, which includes all %{product}-created temporary and build output files, and stops the %{product} server if it is running. When this command completes, it will be safe to execute new commands in the same client, even though the deletion may continue in the background.

flags.name: extension_filter
flags.doc: Only display the usages of these module extensions and the repos generated by them if their respective flags are set. If set, the result graph will only include paths that contain modules using the specified extensions. An empty list disables the filter, effectively specifying all possible extensions.

flags.name: extension_info
flags.doc:
Specify how much detail about extension usages to include in the query result.
- `hidden` will not show any extension information.
- `usages` will only show the extensions names.
- `repos` will also include repos imported with `use_repo`.
- `all` will also show the other repositories generated by extensions.

flags.name: extension_usages
flags.doc: Specify modules whose extension usages will be displayed in the show_extension query.

flags.name: extra_classpath
flags.doc: A colon-separated list of classpath entries to be added to the classpath of the Bazel server.

flags.name: extra_execution_platforms
flags.doc:
The platforms that are available as execution platforms to run actions.
Platforms can be specified by exact target, or as a target pattern.
These platforms will be considered before those declared in the `WORKSPACE` file by
`register_execution_platforms()`. This option may only be set once; later
instances will override earlier flag settings.

flags.name: extra_toolchains
flags.doc:
The toolchain rules to be considered during toolchain resolution.
Toolchains can be specified by exact target, or as a target pattern.
These toolchains will be considered before those declared in the `WORKSPACE` file
by `register_toolchains()`.

flags.name: extract_data_time
flags.doc: The time in ms spent on extracting the new bazel version.

flags.name: failure_detail_out
flags.doc: If set, specifies a location to write a failure_detail protobuf message if the server experiences a failure and cannot report it via gRPC, as normal. Otherwise, the location will be ${OUTPUT_BASE}/failure_detail.rawproto.

flags.name: fat_apk_cpu
flags.doc: No-op
flags.deprecationWarning: Legacy Android flags have been deprecated. See https://blog.bazel.build/2023/11/15/android-platforms.html for details and migration directions

flags.name: fat_apk_hwasan
flags.doc: No-op flag. Will be removed in a future release.

flags.name: fatal_event_bus_exceptions
flags.doc: Whether or not to exit if an exception is thrown by an internal EventBus handler. No-op if --fatal_async_exceptions_exclusions is available; that flag's behavior is preferentially used.
flags.deprecationWarning: Will be enabled by default and removed soon

flags.name: fdo_instrument
flags.doc: Generate binaries with FDO instrumentation. With Clang/LLVM compiler, it also accepts the directory name under which the raw profile file(s) will be dumped at runtime.

flags.name: fdo_optimize
flags.doc: Use FDO profile information to optimize compilation. Specify the name of a zip file containing a .gcda file tree, an afdo file containing an auto profile, or an LLVM profile file. This flag also accepts files specified as labels (e.g. `//foo/bar:file.afdo` - you may need to add an `exports_files` directive to the corresponding package) and labels pointing to `fdo_profile` targets. This flag will be superseded by the `fdo_profile` rule.

flags.name: fdo_prefetch_hints
flags.doc: Use cache prefetch hints.

flags.name: fdo_profile
flags.doc: The fdo_profile representing the profile to be used for optimization.

flags.name: features
flags.doc:
The given features will be enabled or disabled by default for targets built in the target configuration.
Specifying `-{feature}` will disable the feature. Negative features always override positive ones.
See also `--host_features`.

flags.name: fetch
flags.doc: Allows the command to fetch external dependencies. If set to false, the command will utilize any cached version of the dependency, and if none exists, the command will result in failure.

flags.name: fission
flags.doc: Specifies which compilation modes use fission for C++ compilations and links.  May be any combination of {'fastbuild', 'dbg', 'opt'} or the special values 'yes'  to enable all modes and 'no' to disable all modes.

flags.name: flag_alias
flags.doc:
Sets a shorthand name for a Starlark flag. It takes a single key-value pair in the form
`{key}={value}` as an argument.

flags.name: flaky_test_attempts
flags.doc: Each test will be retried up to the specified number of times in case of any test failure. Tests that required more than one attempt to pass are marked as 'FLAKY' in the test summary. Normally the value specified is just an integer or the string 'default'. If an integer, then all tests will be run up to N times. If 'default', then only a single test attempt will be made for regular tests and three for tests marked explicitly as flaky by their rule (flaky=1 attribute). Alternate syntax: regex_filter@flaky_test_attempts. Where flaky_test_attempts is as above and regex_filter stands for a list of include and exclude regular expression patterns (Also see --runs_per_test). Example: --flaky_test_attempts=//foo/.*,-//foo/bar/.*@3 deflakes all tests in //foo/ except those under foo/bar three times. This option can be passed multiple times. The most recently passed argument that matches takes precedence. If nothing matches, behavior is as if 'default' above.

flags.name: for_command
flags.doc: The command for which the options should be canonicalized.

flags.name: force
flags.doc:
Ignore existing repository if any and force fetch the repository again. Only works when
`--enable_bzlmod` is on.

flags.name: force_ignore_dash_static
flags.doc: noop

flags.name: force_pic
flags.doc: If enabled, all C++ compilations produce position-independent code ("-fPIC"), links prefer PIC pre-built libraries over non-PIC libraries, and links produce position-independent executables ("-pie").

flags.name: force_python
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: force_starlark_stack_trace
flags.doc: If --force_starlark_stack_trace=true, Starlark stace traces will always be printed from calls to fail(), including those normally supressed with fail(..., stack_trace = False)

flags.name: from
flags.doc:
The module(s) starting from which the dependency graph query will be displayed. Check
each query’s description for the exact semantics. Defaults to `<root>`.

flags.name: gc_churning_threshold
flags.doc: At any point after an invocation has been running for at least one minute, if Blaze has spent at least this percentage of the invocation's wall time doing full GCs, Blaze will give up and fail with an OOM. A value of 100 effectively means to never give up for this reason.

flags.name: gc_churning_threshold_if_multiple_top_level_targets
flags.doc: If set to a value in [0, 100] and this is a command that takes top-level targets (e.g. build but not query) and there are multiple such top-level targets, overrides --gc_churning_threshold. Useful to configure more aggressive OOMing behavior (i.e. a lower value than --gc_churning_threshold) when they are multiple top-level targets so that the invoker of Bazel can split and retry while still having less aggressive behavior when there is a single top-level target.

flags.name: gc_thrashing_limits
flags.doc: Limits which, if reached, cause GcThrashingDetector to crash Bazel with an OOM. Each limit is specified as <period>:<count> where period is a duration and count is a positive integer. If more than --gc_thrashing_threshold percent of tenured space (old gen heap) remains occupied after <count> consecutive full GCs within <period>, an OOM is triggered. Multiple limits can be specified separated by commas.

flags.name: gc_thrashing_threshold
flags.doc: The percent of tenured space occupied (0-100) above which GcThrashingDetector considers memory pressure events against its limits (--gc_thrashing_limits). If set to 100, GcThrashingDetector is disabled.

flags.name: generate_json_trace_profile
flags.doc: If enabled, Bazel profiles the build and writes a JSON-format profile into a file in the output base. View profile by loading into chrome://tracing. By default Bazel writes the profile for all build-like commands and query.

flags.name: genrule_strategy
flags.doc: Specify how to execute genrules. This flag will be phased out. Instead, use --spawn_strategy=<value> to control all actions or --strategy=Genrule=<value> to control genrules only.

flags.name: gnu_format
flags.doc: If set, write the version to stdout using the conventions described in the GNU standards.

flags.name: google_auth_scopes
flags.doc: A comma-separated list of Google Cloud authentication scopes.

flags.name: google_credentials
flags.doc: Specifies the file to get authentication credentials from. See https://cloud.google.com/docs/authentication for details.

flags.name: google_default_credentials
flags.doc:
Whether to use 'Google Application Default Credentials' for authentication.
See [Authentication methods at Google - Google Cloud][gc-auth-methods] for details.
Disabled by default.

[gc-auth-methods]: https://cloud.google.com/docs/authentication

flags.name: graph:conditional_edges_limit
flags.doc: The maximum number of condition labels to show. -1 means no truncation and 0 means no annotation. This option is only applicable to --output=graph.

flags.name: graph:factored
flags.doc: If true, then the graph will be emitted 'factored', i.e. topologically-equivalent nodes will be merged together and their labels concatenated. This option is only applicable to --output=graph.

flags.name: graph:node_limit
flags.doc: The maximum length of the label string for a graph node in the output.  Longer labels will be truncated; -1 means no truncation.  This option is only applicable to --output=graph.

flags.name: grpc_keepalive_time
flags.doc:
Configures keep-alive pings for outgoing gRPC connections. If this is set, then Bazel
sends pings after this much time of no read operations on the connection, but
only if there is at least one pending gRPC call. The value 0 disables the keep-alives.

flags.name: grpc_keepalive_timeout
flags.doc:
Configures a keep-alive timeout for outgoing gRPC connections. If keep-alive pings are
enabled with `--grpc_keepalive_time`, then Bazel times out a connection if it does
not receive a ping reply after this much time. Times are treated as second
granularity; it is an error to set a value less than one second. If keep-alive
pings are disabled, then this setting is ignored.

flags.name: grpc_tcp_keepalive
flags.doc:
Whether to enable TCP keep-alive (the SO_KEEPALIVE socket option) for outgoing gRPC
connections. This operates at the transport layer and is independent of the
application-level keep-alive pings configured with `--grpc_keepalive_time`. When enabled,
the keep-alive behavior is controlled by `--grpc_tcp_keepalive_time`,
`--grpc_tcp_keepalive_interval` and `--grpc_tcp_keepalive_count`.

flags.name: grpc_tcp_keepalive_count
flags.doc:
When `--grpc_tcp_keepalive` is enabled, the number of unacknowledged TCP keep-alive probes
to send before considering the connection dead (TCP_KEEPCNT). Has no effect if TCP
keep-alive is disabled.

flags.name: grpc_tcp_keepalive_interval
flags.doc:
When `--grpc_tcp_keepalive` is enabled, the amount of time between successive TCP
keep-alive probes (TCP_KEEPINTVL). Has no effect if TCP keep-alive is disabled.

flags.name: grpc_tcp_keepalive_time
flags.doc:
When `--grpc_tcp_keepalive` is enabled, the amount of idle time on a gRPC connection
before the first TCP keep-alive probe is sent (TCP_KEEPIDLE). Has no effect if TCP
keep-alive is disabled.

flags.name: grte_top
flags.doc: A label to a checked-in libc library. The default value is selected by the crosstool toolchain, and you almost never need to override it.

flags.name: guard_against_concurrent_changes
flags.doc: Set this to 'full' to enable checking the ctime of all input files of an action before uploading it to a remote cache. There may be cases where the Linux kernel delays writing of files, which could cause false positives. The default is 'lite', which only checks source files in the main repository. Setting this to 'off' disables all checks. This is not recommended, as the cache may be polluted when a source file is changed while an action that takes it as an input is executing.

flags.name: heap_dump_on_oom
flags.doc: Whether to manually output a heap dump if an OOM is thrown (including manual OOMs due to reaching --gc_thrashing_limits). The dump will be written to <output_base>/<invocation_id>.heapdump.hprof. This option effectively replaces -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError, which has no effect for manual OOMs.

flags.name: help_verbosity
flags.doc: Select the verbosity of the help command.

flags.name: heuristically_drop_nodes
flags.doc: If true, Blaze will remove FileState and DirectoryListingState nodes after related File and DirectoryListing node is done to save memory. We expect that it is less likely that these nodes will be needed again. If so, the program will re-evaluate them.

flags.name: hide_aspect_results
flags.doc:
Comma-separated list of aspect names to not display in results (see `--show_result`).
Useful for keeping aspects added by wrappers which are typically not interesting
to end users out of console output.

flags.name: high_priority_workers
flags.doc: No-op, will be removed soon.

flags.name: home_rc
flags.doc: Whether or not to look for the home bazelrc file at `$HOME/.bazelrc`

flags.name: host_action_env
flags.doc:
Specifies the set of environment variables available to actions with execution
configurations. Variables can be either specified by `name`, in which case the
value will be taken from the invocation environment, by the `name=value` pair
which sets the value independent of the invocation environment, or by
`=name`, which unsets the variable of that name. This option can
be used multiple times; for options given for the same variable, the latest
wins, options for different variables accumulate.

flags.name: host_compilation_mode
flags.doc:
Specify the mode the tools used during the build will be built in. Values:
`fastbuild`, `dbg`, `opt`.

flags.name: host_compiler
flags.doc: No-op flag. Will be removed in a future release.

flags.name: host_conlyopt
flags.doc: Additional option to pass to the C compiler when compiling C (but not C++) source files in the exec configurations.

flags.name: host_copt
flags.doc: Additional options to pass to the C compiler for tools built in the exec configurations.

flags.name: host_cpu
flags.doc: The host CPU.

flags.name: host_crosstool_top
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: host_cxxopt
flags.doc: Additional options to pass to C++ compiler for tools built in the exec configurations.

flags.name: host_features
flags.doc:
The given features will be enabled or disabled by default for targets built in the exec configuration.
Specifying `-{feature}` will disable the feature. Negative features always override positive ones.

flags.name: host_force_python
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: host_grte_top
flags.doc: If specified, this setting overrides the libc top-level directory (--grte_top) for the exec configuration.

flags.name: host_java_launcher
flags.doc: The Java launcher used by tools that are executed during a build.

flags.name: host_java_toolchain
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: host_javabase
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: host_javacopt

flags.name: host_jvm_args
flags.doc: Flags to pass to the JVM executing Blaze.

flags.name: host_jvm_debug
flags.doc: Convenience option to add some additional JVM startup flags, which cause the JVM to wait during startup until you connect from a JDWP-compliant debugger (like Eclipse) to port 5005.

flags.name: host_jvmopt
flags.doc: Additional options to pass to the Java VM when building tools that are executed during  the build. These options will get added to the VM startup options of each  java_binary target.

flags.name: host_linkopt
flags.doc: Additional option to pass to linker when linking tools in the exec configurations.

flags.name: host_macos_minimum_os
flags.doc: Minimum compatible macOS version for host targets. If unspecified, uses 'macos_sdk_version'.

flags.name: host_per_file_copt
flags.doc: Additional options to selectively pass to the C/C++ compiler when compiling certain files in the exec configurations. This option can be passed multiple times. Syntax: regex_filter@option_1,option_2,...,option_n. Where regex_filter stands for a list of include and exclude regular expression patterns (Also see --instrumentation_filter). option_1 to option_n stand for arbitrary command line options. If an option contains a comma it has to be quoted with a backslash. Options can contain @. Only the first @ is used to split the string. Example: --host_per_file_copt=//foo/.*\.cc,-//foo/bar\.cc@-O0 adds the -O0 command line option to the gcc command line of all cc files in //foo/ except bar.cc.

flags.name: host_platform
flags.doc: The label of a platform rule that describes the host system.

flags.name: http_connector_attempts
flags.doc: The maximum number of attempts for http downloads.

flags.name: http_connector_retry_max_timeout
flags.doc: The maximum timeout for http download retries. With a value of 0, no timeout maximum is defined.

flags.name: http_max_parallel_downloads
flags.doc: The maximum number parallel http downloads.

flags.name: http_timeout_scaling
flags.doc: Scale all timeouts related to http downloads by the given factor

flags.name: idle_server_tasks
flags.doc: Run System.gc() when the server is idle

flags.name: iff_heap_size_greater_than
flags.doc: Iff non-zero, then shutdown will only shut down the server if the total memory (in MB) consumed by the JVM exceeds this value.

flags.name: ignore_all_rc_files
flags.doc: Disables all rc files, regardless of the values of other rc-modifying flags, even if these flags come later in the list of startup options.

flags.name: ignore_dev_dependency
flags.doc:
If true, Bazel ignores `bazel_dep`, `use_extension`, and `include` declared as
`dev_dependency` in the `MODULE.bazel` of the root module. Note that these dev
dependencies are always ignored in the `MODULE.bazel` if it is not the root module,
regardless of the value of this flag.

flags.name: implicit_deps
flags.doc: If enabled, implicit dependencies will be included in the dependency graph over which the query operates. An implicit dependency is one that is not explicitly specified in the BUILD file but added by bazel. For cquery, this option controls filtering resolved toolchains.

flags.name: include_artifacts
flags.doc: Includes names of the action inputs and outputs in the output (potentially large).

flags.name: include_aspects
flags.doc: aquery, cquery: whether to include aspect-generated actions in the output. query: no-op (aspects are always followed).

flags.name: include_builtin
flags.doc: Include built-in modules in the dependency graph. Disabled by default because it is quite noisy.

flags.name: include_commandline
flags.doc: Includes the content of the action command lines in the output (potentially large).

flags.name: include_config_fragments_provider
flags.doc:
INTERNAL BLAZE DEVELOPER FEATURE: If `direct`, all configured targets expose
RequiredConfigFragmentsProvider with the configuration fragments they directly
require.
If `transitive`, they do the same but also include the fragments their
transitive dependencies require. If `off`, the provider is omitted.

If not `off`, this also populates `config_setting`'s
`ConfigMatchingProvider.requiredFragmentOptions` with the fragment options the
`config_setting` requires.

Be careful using this feature: it adds memory to every configured target in the
build.

flags.name: include_file_write_contents
flags.doc: Include the file contents for the FileWrite, SourceSymlinkManifest, and RepoMappingManifest actions (potentially large).

flags.name: include_param_files
flags.doc: Include the content of the param files used in the command (potentially large). Note: Enabling this flag will automatically enable the --include_commandline flag.

flags.name: include_pruned_inputs
flags.doc: Includes action inputs that were pruned during action execution. Only affects actions that discover inputs and have been executed in a previous invocation. Only takes effect if --include_artifacts is also set.

flags.name: include_unused
flags.doc:
The queries will also take into account and display the unused modules, which are not
present in the module resolution graph after selection (due to the
Minimal-Version Selection or override rules). This can have different effects for
each of the query types i.e. include new paths in the `all_paths` command, or extra
dependants in the `explain` command.

flags.name: incompatible_allow_python_version_transitions
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: incompatible_allow_tags_propagation
flags.doc: If set to true, tags will be propagated from a target to the actions' execution requirements; otherwise tags are not propagated. See https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/8830 for details.

flags.name: incompatible_always_check_depset_elements
flags.doc: Check the validity of elements added to depsets, in all constructors. Elements must be immutable, but historically the depset(direct=...) constructor forgot to check. Use tuples instead of lists in depset elements. See https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/10313 for details.

flags.name: incompatible_always_include_files_in_data
flags.doc:
If true, native rules add `DefaultInfo.files` of data dependencies to their runfiles,
which matches the recommended behavior for Starlark rules ([runfiles features to avoid]).

[runfiles features to avoid]: https://bazel.build/extending/rules#runfiles_features_to_avoid

flags.name: incompatible_auto_configure_host_platform
flags.doc: This option is deprecated and has no effect.

flags.name: incompatible_auto_exec_groups
flags.doc:
When enabled, an exec groups is automatically created for each toolchain used by a rule.
For this to work rule needs to specify `toolchain` parameter on its actions. For
more information, see [GH-17134].

[GH-17134]: https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/17134

flags.name: incompatible_autoload_externally
flags.doc:
A comma-separated list of rules (or other symbols) that were previously part of Bazel and which are now to be retrieved from their respective external repositories. This flag is intended to be used to facilitate migration of rules out of Bazel. See also https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/23043.
A symbol that is autoloaded within a file behaves as if its built-into-Bazel definition were replaced by its canonical new definition in an external repository. For a BUILD file, this essentially means implicitly adding a load() statement. For a .bzl file, it's either a load() statement or a change to a field of the `native` object, depending on whether the autoloaded symbol is a rule.
Bazel maintains a hardcoded list of all symbols that may be autoloaded; only those symbols may appear in this flag. For each symbol, Bazel knows the new definition location in an external repository, as well as a set of special-cased repositories that must not autoload it to avoid creating cycles.
A list item of "+foo" in this flag causes symbol foo to be autoloaded, except in foo's exempt repositories, within which the Bazel-defined version of foo is still available.
A list item of "foo" triggers autoloading as above, but the Bazel-defined version of foo is not made available to the excluded repositories. This ensures that foo's external repository does not depend on the old Bazel implementation of foo
A list item of "-foo" does not trigger any autoloading, but makes the Bazel-defined version of foo inaccessible throughout the workspace. This is used to validate that the workspace is ready for foo's definition to be deleted from Bazel.
If a symbol is not named in this flag then it continues to work as normal -- no autoloading is done, nor is the Bazel-defined version suppressed. For configuration see https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/master/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/packages/AutoloadSymbols.java As a shortcut also whole repository may be used, for example +@rules_python will autoload all Python rules.

flags.name: incompatible_avoid_hardcoded_objc_compilation_flags
flags.doc: Prevents Bazel from adding compiler options to Objective-C compilation actions. Options set in the crosstool are still applied.

flags.name: incompatible_bazel_test_exec_run_under
flags.doc:
If enabled, `bazel test --run_under=//:runner` builds `//:runner` in the exec
configuration. If disabled, it builds `//:runner` in the target configuration.
Bazel executes tests on exec machines, so the former is more correct. This
doesn't affect `bazel run`, which always builds `--run_under=//foo` in the
target configuration.

flags.name: incompatible_bep_cpu_from_platform
flags.doc: If specified, the value of the cpu constraint (@platforms//cpu:cpu) of the target platform is used to set the Configuration.cpu and Configuration.platform_name fields in the BEP.

flags.name: incompatible_builtin_objc_strip_action
flags.doc: Whether to emit a strip action as part of objc linking.

flags.name: incompatible_check_external_repo_source_dir_package_boundary
flags.doc: If true, a source directory in an external repository fails the build if it crosses a package boundary into a sub-package, matching the behavior that already applies to source directories in the main repository. If false, such package boundary crossings inside external repositories are not detected.

flags.name: incompatible_check_sharding_support
flags.doc:
If true, Bazel will fail a sharded test if the test runner does not indicate that it
supports sharding by touching the file at the path in `TEST_SHARD_STATUS_FILE`.
If false, a test runner that does not support sharding will lead to all tests
running in each shard.

flags.name: incompatible_check_testonly_for_output_files
flags.doc: If enabled, check testonly for prerequisite targets that are output files by looking up the testonly of the generating rule. This matches visibility checking.

flags.name: incompatible_compact_repo_mapping_manifest
flags.doc:
If enabled, the `{binary}.repo_mapping` file emits a module extension's repo mapping
only once instead of once for each repo generated by the extension that
contributes runfiles.

flags.name: incompatible_config_setting_private_default_visibility
flags.doc: If incompatible_enforce_config_setting_visibility=false, this is a noop. Else, if this flag is false, any config_setting without an explicit visibility attribute is //visibility:public. If this flag is true, config_setting follows the same visibility logic as all other rules. See https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/12933.

flags.name: incompatible_default_to_explicit_init_py
flags.doc: This flag changes the default behavior so that __init__.py files are no longer automatically created in the runfiles of Python targets. Precisely, when a py_binary or py_test target has legacy_create_init set to "auto" (the default), it is treated as false if and only if this flag is set. See https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/10076.

flags.name: incompatible_depset_for_java_output_source_jars
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: incompatible_depset_for_libraries_to_link_getter
flags.doc: No-op

flags.name: incompatible_disable_autoloads_in_main_repo
flags.doc: Controls if the autoloads (set by --incompatible_autoload_externally) are enabled in themain repository. When enabled the rules (or other symbols) that were previously part of Bazel need to have load statements. Use buildifier to add them.

flags.name: incompatible_disable_legacy_cc_provider
flags.doc: No-op flag. Will be removed in a future release.

flags.name: incompatible_disable_legacy_flags_cc_toolchain_api
flags.doc: Flag for disabling the legacy cc_toolchain Starlark API for accessing legacy CROSSTOOL fields.

flags.name: incompatible_disable_native_android_rules
flags.doc: If enabled, direct usage of the native Android rules is disabled. Please use the Starlark Android rules from https://github.com/bazelbuild/rules_android

flags.name: incompatible_disable_native_apple_binary_rule
flags.doc: No-op. Kept here for backwards compatibility.

flags.name: incompatible_disable_native_repo_rules
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: incompatible_disable_nocopts
flags.doc: When enabled, it removes nocopts attribute from C++ rules. See https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/8706 for details.

flags.name: incompatible_disable_non_executable_java_binary
flags.doc: If true, java_binary is always executable. create_executable attribute is removed.

flags.name: incompatible_disable_objc_library_transition
flags.doc: Disable objc_library's custom transition and inherit from the top level target instead (No-op in Bazel)

flags.name: incompatible_disable_select_on
flags.doc: List of flags for which the use in `select()` is disabled.

flags.name: incompatible_disable_starlark_host_transitions
flags.doc: If set to true, rule attributes cannot set 'cfg = "host"'. Rules should set 'cfg = "exec"' instead.

flags.name: incompatible_disable_target_default_provider_fields
flags.doc: If set to true, disable the ability to utilize the default provider via field syntax. Use provider-key syntax instead. For example, instead of using `ctx.attr.dep.files` to access `files`, utilize `ctx.attr.dep[DefaultInfo].files See https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/9014 for details.

flags.name: incompatible_disable_target_provider_fields
flags.doc: No-op

flags.name: incompatible_disable_transitions_on
flags.doc: A comma-separated list of flags that cannot be used in transitions inputs or outputs.

flags.name: incompatible_disallow_ctx_resolve_tools
flags.doc: If set to true, calling the deprecated ctx.resolve_tools API always fails. Uses of this API should be replaced by an executable or tools argument to ctx.actions.run or ctx.actions.run_shell.

flags.name: incompatible_disallow_empty_glob
flags.doc: If set to true, the default value of the `allow_empty` argument of glob() is False.

flags.name: incompatible_disallow_java_import_exports
flags.doc: When enabled, java_import.exports is not supported.

flags.name: incompatible_disallow_legacy_py_provider
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: incompatible_disallow_sdk_frameworks_attributes
flags.doc: If true, disallow sdk_frameworks and weak_sdk_frameworks attributes in objc_library andobjc_import.

flags.name: incompatible_disallow_struct_provider_syntax
flags.doc: No-op

flags.name: incompatible_do_not_split_linking_cmdline
flags.doc: When true, Bazel no longer modifies command line flags used for linking, and also doesn't selectively decide which flags go to the param file and which don't.  See https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/7670 for details.

flags.name: incompatible_dont_collect_native_libraries_in_data
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: incompatible_dont_enable_host_nonhost_crosstool_features
flags.doc: If true, Bazel will not enable 'host' and 'nonhost' features in the c++ toolchain (see https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/7407 for more information).

flags.name: incompatible_dont_use_javasourceinfoprovider
flags.doc: No-op

flags.name: incompatible_enable_android_toolchain_resolution
flags.doc: No-op
flags.deprecationWarning: Legacy Android flags have been deprecated. See https://blog.bazel.build/2023/11/15/android-platforms.html for details and migration directions

flags.name: incompatible_enable_apple_toolchain_resolution
flags.doc: Use toolchain resolution to select the Apple SDK for apple rules (Starlark and native)

flags.name: incompatible_enable_cc_toolchain_resolution
flags.doc: No-op flag. Will be removed in a future release.

flags.name: incompatible_enable_cgo_toolchain_resolution
flags.doc: No-op

flags.name: incompatible_enable_deprecated_label_apis
flags.doc: If enabled, certain deprecated APIs (native.repository_name, Label.workspace_name, Label.workspace_root, Label.relative) can be used.

flags.name: incompatible_enable_profile_by_default
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: incompatible_enable_proto_toolchain_resolution
flags.doc: If true, proto lang rules define toolchains from protobuf repository.

flags.name: incompatible_enforce_config_setting_visibility
flags.doc: If true, enforce config_setting visibility restrictions. If false, every config_setting is visible to every target. See https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/12932.

flags.name: incompatible_enforce_starlark_utf8
flags.doc: If enabled (or set to 'error'), fail if Starlark files are not UTF-8 encoded. If set to 'warning', emit a warning instead. If set to 'off', Bazel assumes that Starlark files are UTF-8 encoded but does not verify this assumption. Note that Starlark files which are not UTF-8 encoded can cause Bazel to behave inconsistently.

flags.name: incompatible_exclude_starlark_flags_from_exec_config
flags.doc: If true, don't propagate starlark flags to the exec transition at default; only propagate starlark flags specified in `--experimental_propagate_custom_flag`.

flags.name: incompatible_exclusive_test_sandboxed
flags.doc:
If true, exclusive tests will run with sandboxed strategy. Add `local` tag to force
an exclusive test run locally

flags.name: incompatible_existing_rules_immutable_view
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: incompatible_fail_on_unknown_attributes
flags.doc: If enabled, targets that have unknown attributes set to None fail.

flags.name: incompatible_filegroup_runfiles_for_data
flags.doc: If true, runfiles of targets listed in the srcs attribute are available to targets that consume the filegroup as a data dependency.

flags.name: incompatible_fix_package_group_reporoot_syntax
flags.doc: In package_group's `packages` attribute, changes the meaning of the value "//..." to refer to all packages in the current repository instead of all packages in any repository. You can use the special value "public" in place of "//..." to obtain the old behavior. This flag requires that --incompatible_package_group_has_public_syntax also be enabled.

flags.name: incompatible_java_info_merge_runtime_module_flags
flags.doc: If set to true, the JavaInfo constructor will merge add_exports and add_opens of runtime_deps in addition to deps and exports.

flags.name: incompatible_legacy_local_fallback
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: incompatible_lexicographical_output
flags.doc: If this option is set, sorts --order_output=auto output in lexicographical order.

flags.name: incompatible_limit_platforms_in_output_dir_to
flags.doc: Added for gradual rollout of --experimental_platform_in_output_dir to non-exec configurations. Takes a comma-separated list of platform labels. If set, --experimental_platform_in_output_dir is only enabled for platforms in this list. Otherwise, --experimental_platform_in_output_dir applies to all platforms.

flags.name: incompatible_load_java_rules_from_bzl
flags.doc: Deprecated no-op.

flags.name: incompatible_load_proto_rules_from_bzl
flags.doc: Deprecated no-op.

flags.name: incompatible_load_python_rules_from_bzl
flags.doc: Deprecated no-op.

flags.name: incompatible_locations_prefers_executable
flags.doc: Whether a target that provides an executable expands to the executable rather than the files in DefaultInfo.files under $(locations ...) expansion if the number of files is not 1.

flags.name: incompatible_macos_set_install_name
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: incompatible_make_thinlto_command_lines_standalone
flags.doc: This flag is a noop and scheduled for removal.

flags.name: incompatible_merge_genfiles_directory
flags.doc: If true, the genfiles directory is folded into the bin directory.

flags.name: incompatible_modify_execution_info_additive
flags.doc:
When enabled, passing multiple `--modify_execution_info` flags is additive.
When disabled, only the last flag is taken into account.

flags.name: incompatible_multi_release_deploy_jars
flags.doc: When enabled, java_binary creates Multi-Release deploy jars.

flags.name: incompatible_new_actions_api
flags.doc: No-op

flags.name: incompatible_no_attr_license
flags.doc: If set to true, disables the function `attr.license`.

flags.name: incompatible_no_implicit_file_export
flags.doc: If set, (used) source files are package private unless exported explicitly. See https://github.com/bazelbuild/proposals/blob/master/designs/2019-10-24-file-visibility.md

flags.name: incompatible_no_implicit_watch_label
flags.doc: If true, then methods on repository_ctx that are passed a Label will no longer automatically watch the file under that label for changes even if watch = "no", and repository_ctx.path no longer causes the returned path to be watched. Use repository_ctx.watch instead.

flags.name: incompatible_no_package_distribs
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: incompatible_no_rule_outputs_param
flags.doc: If set to true, disables the `outputs` parameter of the `rule()` Starlark function.

flags.name: incompatible_objc_alwayslink_by_default
flags.doc: If true, make the default value true for alwayslink attributes in objc_library and objc_import.

flags.name: incompatible_override_toolchain_transition
flags.doc: Deprecated, this is no longer in use and should be removed.
flags.deprecationWarning: This is now always set, please remove this flag.

flags.name: incompatible_package_group_has_public_syntax
flags.doc: In package_group's `packages` attribute, allows writing "public" or "private" to refer to all packages or no packages respectively.

flags.name: incompatible_package_group_includes_double_slash
flags.doc: If enabled, when outputting package_group's `packages` attribute, the leading `//` will not be omitted.

flags.name: incompatible_py2_outputs_are_suffixed
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: incompatible_py3_is_default
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: incompatible_python_disable_py2
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: incompatible_python_disallow_native_rules
flags.doc: When true, an error occurs when using the builtin py_* rules; instead the rule_python rules should be used. See https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/17773 for more information and migration instructions.

flags.name: incompatible_remote_local_fallback_for_remote_cache
flags.doc: Whether --remote_local_fallback applies to --remote_cache.

flags.name: incompatible_remove_binary_profile
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: incompatible_remove_ctx_android_fragment
flags.doc: When true, Android build flags are defined with Android rules (in BUIILD files) and ctx.fragments.android is undefined. This is a migration flag to move all Android flags  from core Bazel to Python rules.

flags.name: incompatible_remove_ctx_bazel_py_fragment
flags.doc: When true, Python build flags are defined with Python rules (in BUIILD files) and the ctx.fragments.bazel_py attribute is not present. This is a migration flag to move all Python flags from core Bazel to Python rules.

flags.name: incompatible_remove_ctx_py_fragment
flags.doc: When true, Python build flags are defined with Python rules (in BUIILD files) and ctx.fragments.py is undefined. This is a migration flag to move all Python flags  from core Bazel to Python rules.

flags.name: incompatible_remove_legacy_whole_archive
flags.doc: If true, Bazel will not link library dependencies as whole archive by default (see https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/7362 for migration instructions).

flags.name: incompatible_remove_old_python_version_api
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: incompatible_repo_env_ignores_action_env
flags.doc: If true, --action_env=NAME=VALUE will no longer affect repository rule and module extension environments.

flags.name: incompatible_require_ctx_in_configure_features
flags.doc: This flag is a noop and scheduled for removal.

flags.name: incompatible_require_javaplugininfo_in_javacommon
flags.doc: When enabled java_common.compile only accepts JavaPluginInfo for plugins.

flags.name: incompatible_require_linker_input_cc_api
flags.doc: No-op

flags.name: incompatible_require_repo_extension_metadata
flags.doc: Require repository rules and module extensions to return explicit metadata. Valid values are `false` to disable the check, `all` to require metadata everywhere, or `root` to require metadata only for repo rules and extensions defined in the root module.

flags.name: incompatible_resolve_select_keys_eagerly
flags.doc: If enabled, string keys in dicts passed to select() in .bzl files are immediately resolved to Labels relative to the file instead of being interpreted relative to the BUILD file they are ultimately loaded from.

flags.name: incompatible_run_shell_command_string
flags.doc: If set to true, the command parameter of actions.run_shell will only accept string

flags.name: incompatible_simplify_unconditional_selects_in_rule_attrs
flags.doc: If true, simplify configurable rule attributes which contain only unconditional selects; for example, if ["a"] + select("//conditions:default", ["b"]) is assigned to a rule attribute, it is stored as ["a", "b"]. This option does not affect attributes of symbolic macros or attribute default values.

flags.name: incompatible_skip_genfiles_symlink
flags.doc:
If set to true, the genfiles symlink will not be created. For more information, see
[GH-8651].

[GH-8651]: https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/8651

flags.name: incompatible_stop_exporting_build_file_path
flags.doc: If set to true, deprecated ctx.build_file_path will not be available. ctx.label.package + '/BUILD' can be used instead.

flags.name: incompatible_stop_exporting_language_modules
flags.doc: If enabled, certain language-specific modules (such as `cc_common`) are unavailable in user .bzl files and may only be called from their respective rules repositories.

flags.name: incompatible_strict_action_env
flags.doc:
If true, Bazel uses an environment with a static value for PATH and does not
inherit `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. Use `--action_env=ENV_VARIABLE` if you want to
inherit specific environment variables from the client, but note that doing so
can prevent cross-user caching if a shared cache is used.

flags.name: incompatible_strip_executable_safely
flags.doc: If true, strip action for executables will use flag -x, which does not break dynamic symbol resolution.

flags.name: incompatible_target_cpu_from_platform
flags.doc:
If specified, the value of the cpu constraint (`@platforms//cpu:cpu`) of
the target platform is used to set the `$(TARGET_CPU)` make variable.

flags.name: incompatible_top_level_aspects_require_providers
flags.doc: No-op

flags.name: incompatible_unambiguous_label_stringification
flags.doc: When true, Bazel will stringify the label @//foo:bar to @//foo:bar, instead of //foo:bar. This only affects the behavior of str(), the % operator, and so on; the behavior of repr() is unchanged. See https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/15916 for more information.

flags.name: incompatible_use_cc_configure_from_rules_cc
flags.doc: When true, Bazel will no longer allow using cc_configure from @bazel_tools. Please see https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/10134 for details and migration instructions.

flags.name: incompatible_use_cpp_compile_header_mnemonic
flags.doc: If enabled, give distinguishing mnemonic to header processing actions

flags.name: incompatible_use_new_cgroup_implementation
flags.doc: If true, use the new implementation for cgroups. The old implementation only supports the memory controller and ignores the value of --experimental_sandbox_limits.

flags.name: incompatible_use_plus_in_repo_names
flags.doc: No-op.

flags.name: incompatible_use_python_toolchains
flags.doc: Deprecated. No-op.

flags.name: incompatible_use_specific_tool_files
flags.doc: Use cc toolchain's compiler_files, as_files, and ar_files as inputs to appropriate actions. See https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/8531

flags.name: incompatible_use_toolchain_resolution_for_java_rules
flags.doc: No-op. Kept here for backwards compatibility.

flags.name: incompatible_validate_top_level_header_inclusions
flags.doc: This flag is a noop and scheduled for removal.

flags.name: incompatible_visibility_private_attributes_at_definition
flags.doc: No-op

flags.name: incremental
flags.doc: Whether to do an incremental install. If true, try to avoid unnecessary additional work by reading the state of the device the code is to be installed on and using that information to avoid unnecessary work. If false (the default), always do a full install.

flags.name: incremental_dexing
flags.doc: Does most of the work for dexing separately for each Jar file.

flags.name: incremental_install_verbosity
flags.doc: The verbosity for incremental install. Set to 1 for debug logging.

flags.name: infer_universe_scope
flags.doc: If set and --universe_scope is unset, then a value of --universe_scope will be inferred as the list of unique target patterns in the query expression. Note that the --universe_scope value inferred for a query expression that uses universe-scoped functions (e.g.`allrdeps`) may not be what you want, so you should use this option only if you know what you are doing. See https://bazel.build/reference/query#sky-query for details and examples. If --universe_scope is set, then this option's value is ignored. Note: this option applies only to `query` (i.e. not `cquery`).

flags.name: info_output_type
flags.doc: If stdout, results are directly printed to the console. If response_proto, the info command results are packed in response extensions.

flags.name: inject_repository
flags.doc:
Adds a new repository with a local path in the form of `{repository name}={path}`. This
only takes effect with `--enable_bzlmod` and is equivalent to adding a
corresponding `local_repository` to the root module's `MODULE.bazel` file via
`use_repo_rule`. If the given path is an absolute path, it will be used as it is.
If the given path is a relative path, it is relative to the current working
directory. If the given path starts with `%workspace%`, it is relative to the
workspace root, which is the output of `bazel info workspace`. If the given path
is empty, then remove any previous injections.

flags.name: install_base
flags.doc: This launcher option is intended for use only by tests.

flags.name: install_md5
flags.doc: This launcher option is intended for use only by tests.

flags.name: instrument_test_targets
flags.doc:
When coverage is enabled, specifies whether to consider instrumenting test rules.
When set, test rules included by `--instrumentation_filter` are instrumented.
Otherwise, test rules are always excluded from coverage instrumentation.

flags.name: instrumentation_filter
flags.doc:
When coverage is enabled, only rules with names included by the
specified regex-based filter will be instrumented. Rules prefixed
with '-' are excluded instead. Note that only non-test rules are
